title: Celine Dion overcomes rare neurological disorder to perform first concert in 6 years
summary: Celine Dion's return to the stage underscored a remarkable comeback after stiff-person syndrome, an incurable condition that causes stiffness and cramps, forced her to cancel shows and cast years of uncertainty over whether she would ever perform again.
story: Celine Dion wept tears of joy on Saturday as she fulfilled her dream of returning to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder, with a sold-out concert in Paris.

The 58-year-old French Canadian singer appeared visibly moved as she opened her first full concert in six years with her 1990s French-language ballad "On ne change pas" ("One Doesn't Change"), singing to a crowd of 30,000 enthralled fans.
"These are, of course, tears of joy. I'm so delighted to see you," Dion said, blowing kisses to the audience at the packed Plenitude Arena on the western edge of Paris.

Her return to the stage underscored a remarkable comeback after stiff-person syndrome, an incurable condition that causes stiffness and cramps, forced her to cancel shows and cast years of uncertainty over whether she would ever perform again.
"The path was rockier than expected," she said, speaking in French and English.
"But I held on to a faint ray of light in the distance, deep in the mountains."
"Tonight, I want to sing for you, sing for myself, sing for life," she added.
The largely female crowd sported sequined dresses and tops, glittered cheeks and T-shirts emblazoned with the star's image or nods to her biggest hits.
"It's unreal to be here!" said Elisabeth Landry, a 38-year-old Quebecer who lives near the star's hometown of Charlemagne.
"I was convinced we'd never see her again, especially not embarking on a run of concerts like this."
French daily Le Parisien said former first lady Michelle Obama was "discreetly attending this first concert."
Just hours before, one of the best-selling singers of all time greeted admirers outside her luxury hotel a short walk from the Arc de Triomphe.
Albertina Cabral, a fan from the Brazilian city of Sao Paulo, said she could barely put her feelings into words.
"It's unbelievable to stay here and to go to the concert and to see Celine so close," she said. "And she's feeling good, she's happy."
Paris spared no effort in welcoming Dion, drawing thousands of fans from across the world, including some who flew in from as far away as the French Polynesian island of Tahiti.
For days, Paris played host to costume contests, giant karaoke parties and tribute cruises on the Seine.

On Friday, the iconic cauldron rose above the Tuileries Garden, echoing the diva's surprise appearance up the Eiffel Tower to perform "Hymn to Love" by Edith Piaf during the opening ceremony of the Paris Olympics in 2024.
A lyric from the song, "I'd go and fetch the moon if you asked me to," along with the singer's first name, was projected in big letters onto the balloon.
The suburban train station serving the arena has been temporarily renamed "Celine."
Chloe and Katy Rydquist, who traveled from London, had spent around $2,000 on their tickets, saying Dion's return to the stage justified the cost.
"She's a legend," Chloe said.
The star's residency is projected to generate hundreds of millions of euros in economic benefits.
She kicks off her 26-date run with 16 sold-out shows in September and October, before returning for another 10 in May.
Fans who missed out on tickets have found other ways to catch a glimpse of their idol.
Dion has regularly stepped outside the Royal Monceau hotel to greet waiting fans, at times breaking into song and dance with them well into the early hours.
Over her four-decade career, Dion has sold around 260 million albums in English and French, with hits including "It's All Coming Back to Me Now" and "Because You Loved Me."

Dion revealed in late 2022 that she had been diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome. According to the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, the rare disorder is believed to be an autoimmune condition in which your immune system attacks the healthy cells of your body by mistake.
It can cause "stiff muscles in the torso, arms, and legs," as well as "greater sensitivity to noise, touch, and emotional distress, which can set off muscle spasms," according to the NIH.
It impacts twice as many women as men, the NIH said, and is also believed to be a progressive disorder that worsens over time. While symptoms can be treated with medication, there is no cure.
According to the Johns Hopkins Stiff-Person Syndrome Center, the disorder is estimated to impact only one to two people per one million in population.
Dion has described it as making her feel as though she is being strangled, with cramps so intense they have left her with broken ribs.
She has returned to the stage after what she has described as years of training "like an athlete," doing ballet and Pilates several times a week, as well as voice therapy.

title: Alexander Zverev wins U.S. Open, beating American Ben Shelton
summary: Germany's Alexander Zverev won his second Grand Slam after finally taking home his first major title earlier this year at the French Open.
story: Alexander Zverev dispatched Ben Shelton in four sets to win the U.S. Open men's singles title on Sunday, the second Grand Slam win for the German after he finally broke through at the French Open earlier this year.

The No. 1 seed in a Grand Slam for the first time, Zverev capitalized on Shelton's shaky start in his first major final, played a nearly flawless tiebreaker on serve and then turned back Shelton's comeback attempt to win 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2  in front of a crowd that desperately cheered the American on.

After taking down his fellow countryman Francis Tiafoe in a thrilling semifinal, Shelton was aiming to become the first American man to win a major since Andy Roddick's U.S. Open victory in 2003. Shelton was also the first Black American man to make it to a U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972.
"You're one of the very best players in the world, maybe the best player in the world this year," Shelton told Zverev during the trophy ceremony.

But Zverev was too good in majors this year and apparently didn't even know how good he was. He finished the match on his serve but didn't seem to realize it, dropping back behind the baseline as if set to return. Only a few moments later did he figure out he had won, raising his arms in celebration.

"I know today 99.9% of the people wanted Ben to win, so I'm very sorry, first of all," Zverev said during the trophy presentation. "But second, it was an incredible atmosphere to play in. Even though I know that the crowd was against me, the crowd was always incredibly fair."
Zverev improved to 25-2 in major matches this year and won $5.5 million on Sunday, matching the prize earned by women's champion Elena Rybakina on Saturday as the largest in Grand Slam history.

He thought this title would come in 2020 and still acknowledges it should have. He won the first two sets against Dominic Thiem and got within two points of victory before becoming the first man to blow a two-set lead and lose in the final since 1949.
Whatever ghosts were left from then are long gone now.
Zverev also reached the final at Wimbledon, falling to Jannik Sinner, and became the No. 1 seed in New York when the top-ranked Sinner had to withdraw with a knee injury.
"I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before," Zverev said, addressing his team.
Shelton had already eliminated the defending champion when he beat Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set quarterfinal that ended at 3:33 a.m., the latest finish in U.S. Open history.
But he fell short on Sunday in his attempt to become the first man to beat the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds en route to the U.S. Open title since 1975.
The No. 8 seed fell to 0-6 against Zverev, winning a set Sunday for only the second time.
The 23-year-old Shelton figures to get more chances, but Americans who have grown tired of waiting to celebrate a men's title wanted it now.

Fans stood and screamed when Shelton emerged from the tunnel before the match, but he didn't give them any reason to keep the cheers going once play began. Serving first, he lost the opening two points and then eventually handed the game to Zverev with a double fault.
Zverev maintained that lead the rest of the set, which ended on another double-fault by Shelton.
Zverev's deliberate playing style helped limit the crowd's effectiveness. Fans are expected to quiet down as a player is preparing to serve and stay quiet until the ensuing point has been completed.

Zverev bounces the ball a number of times — sometimes around 10, maybe a dozen, others nearly 20, insisting there is no set pattern or plan — before he begins his toss, so it guarantees lengthy stretches of silence.

Fans tried to get around that by occasionally cheering when he missed a first serve — another tennis no-no that the chair umpire scolded them for — but Zverev, who said before the match he enjoyed hostile crowds, did not seem affected.
Zverev then turned back Shelton's chance to even the match in the tiebreaker.

Shelton returned Zverev's opening serve long, was beaten by a superb passing shot and then came up on the wrong end of a 16-shot rally as Zverev went up 3-0. Zverev then hit serves of 147 mph and 124 mph that Shelton couldn't get back in play. Shelton cut it to 5-2 and then got a return in play for the only time, but Zverev won the point and then hit another serve at 139 mph to close it out.

title: Sweden's election exit polls show center-left opposition ahead of populist right
summary: The election pits Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's center-right coalition against a center-left bloc led by former Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrats.
story: Across Europe, right-wing populist parties have gained ground in recent years amid growing voter backlash over immigration. Sweden has been no exception, but exit polls from Sunday's elections show voters are favoring the center-left opposition.

The election pits Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's center-right coalition against a center-left bloc led by former Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrats. The polls from Swedish public broadcaster SVT project Andersson's four-party group winning a majority, paving the way for her to return to office pending coalition talks, the Associated Press reported.
The first preliminary results were expected Sunday evening from election officials.
Hanging over the race is the prospect of Sweden's right-wing populist Sweden Democrats entering government for the first time.

The party, which traces its roots to Sweden's extreme-right fringe, has spent the past two decades moving steadily toward the center of political power. It first entered parliament in 2010. By 2022, it became the country's second-largest party and agreed to support Kristersson's minority government from outside the cabinet. The arrangement gave the party substantial influence over immigration, crime and other policies without formal responsibility for government departments. But now Kristersson wants to govern as a majority government and has gone one step further, saying the Sweden Democrats would receive ministerial posts if the right wins another term.

This has transformed the election into a test of the Sweden Democrats' long political normalization and whether Swedish voters are prepared to see a party once shunned by almost the entire political establishment now exercise executive power.

"There has been a shift of focus, which has gone from the true political challenges to who is going to sit in the government," Andreas Önnerfors, a professor of intellectual history at Linnaeus University, told CBS News.
The polls are currently on a knife-edge, with an Indikator Opinion poll conducted Sept. 2–10 putting the center-left coalition on 50.8%, against 47.6% for the right coalition.
From fringe to mainstream

For years, Sweden's established parties maintained what amounted to a political firewall around the Sweden Democrats because of the party's extremist roots. As recently as 2018, Kristersson assured Holocaust survivor Hédi Fried that he would not cooperate with the party, according to Reuters. The Sweden Democrats themselves acknowledge that figures involved in their early history had connections to neo-Nazi and white supremacist movements.

But under Jimmie Åkesson, who has led the party since 2005, the Sweden Democrats have sought to expel extremists, moderate their image and present themselves as a mainstream right-wing party, with policies including deporting people who are in the country illegally, toughening citizenship laws, requiring strict assimilation of newcomers and restricting social security to citizens.
Part of the party's success has come from combining positions traditionally associated with the political right with policies aimed at working-class voters.

"They have merged typical right-wing positions with typical Labour or Social Democratic positions — social security and benefits and things like that. That makes sense among ordinary people," Önnerfors said.
Immigration and crime as key voter concerns

The Sweden Democrats helped make tougher immigration and crime policies central to Swedish politics. Still, their durability is also rooted in profound changes in Swedish society and voters' perceptions.

"Swedish politics has clearly moved in a more restrictive direction on issues such as immigration and crime," Professor Niklas Bolin, a political scientist at Mid Sweden University, told CBS News. "Importantly, this shift is not limited to the parties on the right. The Social Democrats, Sweden's largest party, have also moved in this direction."

Sweden received around 163,000 asylum applications during the 2015 European migration crisis; with a population just shy of 11 million, it was among the highest per-capita rates in Europe. In subsequent years, integration, segregation and a surge in gang shootings and bombings became major national political issues. The country's approach to immigration has since changed dramatically.
The Swedish government says asylum immigration has fallen to its lowest level since 1985.

Government policies on crime have also led gang violence to recede. Police figures show shootings falling from 391 in 2022 to 158 in 2025, with the decline continuing this year. But the political consequences of the violence and the wider debate over immigration and integration have endured.
"The Sweden Democrats have built a stable electoral base," Bolin said.
"Immigration and dissatisfaction with integration remain important explanations, but their support is also linked to concerns about crime and a broader dissatisfaction with established parties."
Their support, he added, is "particularly strong among men, working-class voters and voters outside the larger cities."

For a country that for generations has prided itself on low crime, a generous welfare state and liberal attitudes toward immigration, equality and individual rights, Sunday's election marks an important moment — testing how far Sweden's politics have shifted, and whether a party once kept at the margins is now ready to enter the heart of government.

title: Trump says Ukraine needs to stop targeting Russian refineries
summary: Civilians were killed and injured overnight into Sunday as both Russia and Ukraine kept up large-scale drone strikes.
story: President Trump on Sunday called on his Ukrainian counterpart to halt strikes on Russian refineries, saying the attacks are causing a shortage of diesel.

Mr. Trump, who is in Ireland watching the Irish Open at one of his golf courses for the weekend, was asked by a reporter if he had spoken with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy following his recent conversation with Russia's Vladimir Putin. The U.S. president responded by calling on Zelenskyy to halt strikes against Russia.
"Mr. Zelensky has to do one thing. He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Mr. Trump said. "Let him go after targets but not diesel fuel, because he's causing a shortage of diesel fuel."

Ukraine's recent long-range strikes have targeted Russia's oil and gas industry, which Kyiv says both funds and directly fuels its war on Ukraine. The Ukrainian drone campaign has caused fuel rationing across Russia, despite the country being a key oil and gas exporter. Other Ukrainian strikes targeted major Russian online retailers, bringing the war ever closer to the public.
Mr. Trump's remarks come as Russia and Ukraine continued overnight waves of drone attacks.

Two people were killed in Russia's Tatarstan, according to local officials. At the same time, Ukrainian authorities reported Russian drone attacks on the Black Sea port of Odesa and a fire near a border crossing with Poland.

Russia has ramped up its air campaign in recent weeks, using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones to pierce Ukraine's defenses and capitalize on Kyiv's dwindling stock of missile interceptors. Moscow's attacks have targeted Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter in what officials say is meant to demoralize civilians.
Russia hits train shortly after Western officials passed

A Russian drone targeted a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after trains with top Western figures — including ex-CIA Director David Petraeus, former U.K. Prime Minister Boris Johnson and former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt— passed through, Ukraine's rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia said in a statement.

No casualties were reported after the Russian strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said. Russia said it struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine.

"Quite possibly, the target of this drone could have been the diplomatic train, which had left the station earlier than expected because of the timetable change... due to constant threats of Russian strikes," Ukrzaliznytsia said.
CBS News partner BBC News said Johnson, Petraeu and other European senior security advisers passed along the same train line on their way back from a conference in Kyiv.
Johnson condemned the attack as "random and senseless" in a post on social media.

"I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning," Johnson said. He asked, "When are we going to give them the air defences they need?"
Russia said Sunday it struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine used to "transport military cargo" from Europe, Agence France-Presse reported.

"Strikes have continued on railway infrastructure in the western regions of Ukraine, which are used to transport military cargo from European countries," Moscow's defense ministry said in a statement.
Kremlin open to restarting peace talks
On Sunday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow is open to restarting peace talks in the autumn featuring Russia, Ukraine and the U.S.
"We are not ruling out that possibility. We are specifically talking about the foreseeable future. That is, October cannot be ruled out," Peskov told reporters.

Last weekend, U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held talks with Putin in Moscow, followed by a meeting with Zelenskyy in Kyiv. Despite the latest diplomatic push, Moscow and Kyiv's core demands remain mutually exclusive, especially over territorial concessions.
Kushner, who is Mr. Trump's son-in-law, said Sunday that "territory is going to be the main issue, and, you know, that's where the sides are still apart."

"Our job as the mediator is to figure out how can we come up with a creative solution that doesn't violate [Ukraine's] desires and that helps them achieve, you know, their objective and does it in a way that we can get Russia to end the conflict in a way that hopefully, you know, allows both parties to move forward in a framework where this doesn't happen again," Kushner said.

title: Search underway for 130 people after Indonesian passenger ship overturns
summary: Indonesian rescuers launched a search operation after authorities lost contact with a passenger ship carrying more than 240 people in the Java Sea.
story: A ferry overturned in bad weather in Indonesia's Java Sea on Sunday, leaving about 130 passengers and crew missing, rescuers said. At least 107 people were rescued and the bodies of six passengers were recovered as the search operation expanded around the vessel's last known position.
The ferry with more than 240 people was traveling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan province, on Borneo Island, officials said.

The vessel's captain had reported rough seas with waves up to 10 feet before issuing a distress call, saying the ship was listing, said I Putu Sudayana, who heads the Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office. Authorities later received information indicating the vessel had overturned.
The rescue agency in Banjarmasin said it received a report two hours after contact was lost with the Virgo Transport 8 at about 2 a.m. Sunday.

A rescue ship was headed to the vessel's last known position, he said, and by Sunday afternoon authorities were deploying teams supported by eight vessels, including four navy ship, and two helicopters.

Initial information indicated the vessel's last known position was in the Java Sea, about 92 miles from Banjarmasin. The ship's manifest said it was carrying 243 people - 213 passengers and 30 crew members - although it is common in Indonesia for the number of passengers to differ from the manifest. The vessel was also transporting 89 vehicles.

Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said aerial searches showed the ferry was floating upside down and had not sunk. Rescuers were concentrating search efforts around the overturned ferry, he told reporters Sunday.

Hundreds of relatives gathered at a command center in Banjarmasin's Trisakti port, awaiting word on family members believed to be aboard the ferry. Many anxiously checked passenger manifests and rescue lists as authorities continued searching for survivors.
"I was shocked when I saw my uncle's name on the passenger list," said a woman who goes by a single name, Bunga. "But I felt relieved after officials told me he had been rescued."
Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands where ferries are a common method of travel. Disasters occur regularly, with weak safety enforcement often blamed.

title: 2026 Emmy Awards: Winners and losers
summary: Matthew Rhys made Emmy Awards history by winning two lead acting awards in one ceremony, but the full list of winners holds even more surprises.
story: Matthew Rhys told Fox News Digital that he plans on having a "wild" night after the 78th Annual Emmy Awards.
The 78th Emmy Awards took place Monday night at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Mariska Hargitay hosting the ceremony – the first woman to host the award show in 15 years.
"The Pitt" led all programs with 25 nominations, while "Hacks" earned a record 24 nominations during its final season. Apple TV’s "Widow’s Bay" followed with 19 nominations, and "Pluribus" had 18.

The Creative Arts Emmys were presented ahead of Monday night, with notable wins for Shailene Woodley, Mariska Hargitay, Bad Bunny and the late Rob Reiner. "Widow’s Bay" led the early awards with eight wins, while "DTF St. Louis" earned six.
Mariska Hargitay appeared at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, which she hosted. (Trae Patton/NBC via Getty Images)

Matthew Rhys made Emmy history Monday night by winning two lead acting awards in the same ceremony. The actor first won outstanding lead actor in a limited or anthology series for Netflix’s "The Beast in Me" before taking home outstanding lead actor in a comedy series for Apple TV’s "Widow’s Bay."

title: Dolly Parton, Rob Reiner receive emotional tributes during 2026 Emmy Awards
summary: Sally Field delivered an emotional tribute to Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmy Awards, calling her "Steel Magnolias" co-star an angel on earth.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Sally Field reflected on Dolly Parton's legacy during a moving tribute to the late country music legend at the 2026 Emmy Awards in Los Angeles, Calif.
"If there are truly angels on earth, then we just lost one, Dolly Parton," Field confessed of her "Steel Magnolias" co-star.
Parton died on Aug. 25 following a "brief battle with cancer," according to her representatives. She was 80.
DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY
Dolly Parton and Rob Reiner were each honored during the 78th Emmy Awards in Los Angeles, Calif., on Monday. (Getty Images)

"It was my great, good fortune to have worked with Dolly in a film called 'Steel Magnolias,' and over the years I never stopped loving her though we lived very far apart," Field told the audience at the Peacock Theater. "I adored her from day one, how could you not?"
"She was genuine, and humble, supportive and blisteringly funny with a bawdy sense of humor that would send any rude guy looking for a place to hide."
CARRIE UNDERWOOD HONORS DOLLY PARTON'S FAITH AND LEGACY DURING EMOTIONAL CONCERT TRIBUTE
Reba McEntire performed a rendition of Parton's '83 hit, "Appalachian Memories." (Patrick T. Fallon)
Field, 79, admitted that she "couldn't see then what a real giant Dolly was."

"Not just as an artist, but as a human ... She was a humanitarian whose contributions had made a profound difference in the lives of so many in her home state of Tennessee, and across our country," Field said.
"God bless you, Dolly Parton, my friend. I am not the only one on earth that will love you forever and ever."
Dolly Parton died in August after a brief battle with cancer. (ABC Photo Archives)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Dressed in a sparkling white gown, Reba McEntire then took the stage to perform a rendition of Parton's classic 1983 song, "Appalachian Memories."
Parton was surrounded by loved ones at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center when she died peacefully in Nashville, Tenn., last month.
With Noah Kahan leading a rendition of "Bridge Over Troubled Water," Jamie Lee Curtis commemorated the life of director Rob Reiner, who died in December alongside his wife, Michele Singer Reiner.
Jamie Lee Curtis remembered the late director Rob Reiner at the 2026 Emmy Awards. (Patrick T. Fallon)
Rob Reiner, his wife Michele Singer and son Nick Reiner in 2013. (Michael Buckner/Getty Images for Teen Vogue)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Their 32-year-old son, Nick Reiner, was indicted last month on two counts of first-degree murder with special circumstances which make him eligible for the death penalty.
"Last year we lost another cherished legend, our beloved 'Meathead,' Rob Reiner," Curtis said. "He was generous and kind and funny as hell and a friend to all."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Jake Reiner, Romy Reiner, Rob Reiner and Michele Reiner pictured in 2024. (Neilson Barnard/Getty Images)
During last week's Creative Arts Emmys, Reiner received a posthumous Emmy for his guest role in "The Bear."
"He now holds the record of 48 years for the longest gap between acting Emmys, which was previously held by his father Carl Reiner at 37 years," Curtis told the crowd through tears.
Macaulay Culkin, Annie Murphy and Dan Levy paid tribute to the late Catherine O'Hara during the 78th Emmy Awards. The "Home Alone" actress died in January following a brief illness. She was 71.
"Home Alone" star Macaulay Culkin remembered his on-screen mother Catherine O'Hara during a tribute with her "Schitt's Creek" co-stars Dan Levy and Annie Murphy. (Patrick T. Fallon)
"There are all kinds of words I could use to describe Catherine," Culkin said. "She was encouraging, she was warm, she was funny. But the word that I think of is mama."
He added, "By the way, call your mother tonight. For real."

title: Michael J Fox receives standing ovation at 2026 Emmys for Parkinson's disease advocacy work
summary: Michael J. Fox received a standing ovation at the 2026 Emmys alongside wife Tracy Pollan, revealing his foundation is "close" to a Parkinson's cure.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Michael J. Fox was honored with the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the 2026 Emmys for his advocacy and philanthropic work supporting Parkinson’s disease research.

The Bob Hope Humanitarian Award is an honorary Emmy presented by the Television Academy and the Bob & Dolores Hope Foundation. Established in 2002, it recognizes a television-industry figure whose philanthropic work has made a lasting impact on society.
Fox attended the award show on Monday night with his wife, Tracy Pollan. This was the couple's first appearance at the Emmy Awards in 13 years.
Michael J. Fox at the 78th Emmy Awards held at Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026, in Los Angeles, California. (Rich Polk/Variety via Getty Images)

Fox received a standing ovation as he took the stage and talked about his Parkinson’s diagnosis. Fox was diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson’s disease in 1991 at age 29. He publicly revealed his diagnosis in 1998.
MARISKA HARGITAY, SELENA GOMEZ AND ZENDAYA STUN AT 2026 EMMYS: VOTE ON YOUR FAVORITE TV STAR LOOKS
On the Emmy Awards' stage, Fox said, "Initially, I kept my Parkinson's diagnosis a secret. I worried that it would affect my work and my relationship with audiences."
Michael J. Fox accepts the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award. (NBC via Getty Images)

He continued, "Would they laugh if they knew I was sick? And then I was stunned by the support I got. The support from all of you. It was so uplifting. It made me feel like I could keep doing this, and I hadn't lost what I do, and they couldn't take this away from me. And it's because you stood up for me, and I really appreciate it."

title: Prince Harry's homecoming goes off the rails with brutal TV roast
summary: "Saturday Night Live UK" skewered Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to the U.K., mocking their Netflix deal and royal family tensions.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were barely back on British soil before "Saturday Night Live UK" rolled out an unforgiving royal welcome.

The royal couple became the target of a string of jokes on the British version of the iconic sketch comedy show, which poked fun at their relationship with the royal family, lucrative Netflix deal and Markle’s lifestyle brand as the pair settled back into life across the pond.
The sketch opened with King Charles III and Queen Camilla enjoying a seemingly peaceful weekend at Balmoral before their royal retreat took an unexpected turn.
KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle found themselves at the center of a biting "Saturday Night Live UK" sketch just weeks after relocating to Britain. (Getty Images)
"Oh, Camilla, nothing like a quiet Saturday in Balmoral. Clean Scottish air, dirty Scottish people … bliss," the King, portrayed by Larry Dean, said.
"I do so love our weekends away," Camilla, played by Emma Sidi, added. "No responsibilities – just like every other day."
Their quiet moment was interrupted by Prince Harry, portrayed by Jack Shep, and Markle, portrayed by Ayoade Bamgboye.
"Daddy, I’m home," Prince Harry said as the two walked into the room.
The show didn't miss a beat, immediately making jokes regarding Markle's Netflix show "With Love, Meghan." Markle's character brought an ice tray as a "gift" for Queen Camilla.

"It’s ice. I made it myself. I can give you the recipe. I’m kind of a wiz in the kitchen," Markle's character said in the skit.
"It’s true. She hires the best cooks," the fake Prince Harry added.
As Prince Harry and Markle packed on the PDA, King Charles began to question the two about their motives for moving back to the U.K.
"Don’t tell me you spent all your Netflix money already," Dean as King Charles joked.
"Daddy, it was $60 million! How long was it meant to last?" the fake Prince Harry whined.

Markle and Prince Harry moved back to the U.K. in late August.

The couple’s children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, have already enrolled at British schools and will start classes sometime in September. The family plans to live at a private, nonroyal residence outside of London, but haven’t said exactly where that will be.
However, the couple's return home didn't come with a royal reset.

Buckingham Palace drew a firm line around the Sussexes’ homecoming, reaffirming that the couple will not resume official duties and that their status remains unchanged from when they stepped back as working royals in 2020.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family," a letter sent on behalf of King Charles III read, Fox News confirmed. title: Macklemore doubles down after getting kicked off Ed Sheeran tour after pro-Palestine stance
summary: Macklemore claims Robert Kraft rallied stadium owners to give Ed Sheeran an ultimatum over his "Free Palestine" remarks on the U.S. Loop Tour.
story: Podcaster Bethany Mandel joins 'Fox & Friends' to react to rapper Macklemore's anti-Israel and anti-America rants delivered during live stage performances. Mandel also addresses the growing outrage among concertgoers.

A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Ed Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's "Loop Tour."

"As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."
Macklemore was slated to appear at eight of the 10 shows left on the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour.
PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS
Macklemore was kicked off Ed Sheeran's stadium tour after his "Free Palestine" remarks. (Getty Images)
On Monday, Macklemore addressed the announcement and doubled down on his stance.

"I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth," he wrote in a lengthy Instagram statement. "Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour. But before I get into it, I want to say something that should be obvious. In this moment I think it matters. I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families."
Pink received backlash after reposting a video criticizing Macklemore following his comments on Palestine and Israel.  (John Nacion/Variety via Getty Images; Kristy Sparow/Getty Images)
BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM

"The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence. More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don’t lose sight of that."
WATCH: MACKLEMORE OPENED HIS PERFORMANCE WITH AN ANTI-ICE AND ISRAEL RANT

On Sept. 4, Macklemore opened for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. He repeatedly chanted "Free Palestine" while a slideshow played on the screen behind him, showing footage from the war in Gaza.

Several fans were upset by the performance, including an Instagram page called "Stop Antisemitism." The page shared a video criticizing Macklemore, calling the move "awful." Pink reposted the video to her own Instagram story, which started a new wave of backlash from people criticizing her for seemingly being pro-Israel.
In his Instagram post, Macklemore said he and Sheeran, who he considers a "friend" and "brother," had "some difficult conversations" in the days following his remarks.

"The type of talks rooted in love and respect for one another that still end in a place of fundamental disagreement," he wrote. "Nothing I’m writing here is out of spite or because I want to tear down his character. But as I told Ed multiple times on the phone, our friendship can’t change my responsibility to tell the truth about what happened."
Macklemore performs during night one of Ed Sheeran’s concert at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Fox News Digital)

The rapper claimed Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, told Sheeran that Macklemore "would not be allowed" to perform at the stadium.
Kraft issued a statement defending his decision to influence the rapper's removal from the tour.

"Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," the statement read.

"Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line."
Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots, defended his decision to influence Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's tour. (Bryan Bennett/Getty Images)

The statement continued: "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I agree with Macklemore. Too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate. Over many decades, I have directed resources to Palestine and created athletic and entrepreneurial opportunities for Palestinians who I admire and respect. Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive.

"Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed. I have tremendous respect for Ed and his music, particularly his unique ability to bring people together and spread joy, and I have always been proud to welcome him and his fans to Gillette Stadium.
"I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."
Macklemore has been vocal about his stance on Palestine for years.  (ARNAUD FINISTRE / AFP via Getty Images)

In Macklemore's post, he said, "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

"Ed was in a f---ed up position," he wrote. "He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public facing, 'I don’t take sides.'"

CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT
Macklemore said he's been saying "Free Palestine" onstage for almost three years and questioned why he was being removed from the tour now.

"What I said at MetLife I have been saying on stages around the world for almost three years. So why is it an issue now? Because now I’m sharing a stage with one of the biggest artists in the world, in some of the biggest stadiums in America. At a certain level of exposure, ‘Free Palestine’ becomes too much of a risk. If I kept doing the shows, saying ‘Free Palestine,’ with Ed implicitly supporting it, the crowd getting loud and showing undeniable support for Palestinian liberation, what artist might speak out next? The stage becomes resistance. Maybe that’s why this time it became so important to silence me."

"And one of the most effective ways to enforce that silence has been to weaponize the accusation of antisemitism. Antisemitism is real," he continued. "And that is exactly why the word matters too much to be used as a shield against criticism of the Israeli state. When criticizing Israel, opposing Zionism or saying ‘Free Palestine’ gets conflated with hatred of Jewish people, it doesn’t protect Jewish people. It protects Israel from accountability."
While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he said he stands by his position.

DeVito recalled cast members and celebrity guests spilling into all-night "ragers" where music blared until sunrise and, as he put it, there was "crudité and cocaine."

title: Bob Mackie, legendary designer who dressed Cher, Tina Turner and Dolly Parton, dead at 87
summary: Bob Mackie's iconic designs for Cher, Carol Burnett and Diana Ross shaped Hollywood glamour, while stars like Sabrina Carpenter revived his archives.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Bob Mackie, the legendary fashion and costume designer known for dressing some of the biggest stars, died Monday. He was 87.
Mackie died of pneumonia, his representative confirmed to Fox News Digital.

"It is with a heavy heart that we share the news that Mr. Bob Mackie passed away today," a post shared on his official Instagram read. "He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a Fashion and Costume Designer, which is all he ever wanted to do."
"His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world," the statement concluded.
HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026
Cher and Bob Mackie at Diana Vreeland's 14th Annual Costume Exhibit. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
He is survived by his granddaughter Alyssa Townsend, his great-granddaughters Kyla and Keira Townsend and his former wife, Lulu Porter.
Mackie was known for his glittering, theatrical creations that helped define the looks of stars such as Cher, Carol Burnett, Diana Ross, Dolly Parton and Tina Turner.

His career took off after he began designing for Mitzi Gaynor and then landed the job of creating costumes for "The Carol Burnett Show," remaining with the variety series throughout its 11-season run.

"Throughout his extraordinary body of work, Bob Mackie understood the unique power of costume in comedy – to help create a character and become part of the creative energy that drove the comedy itself," National Comedy Center Executive Director Journey Gunderson told Fox News Digital.

"His work with Carol Burnett and the ensemble of ‘The Carol Burnett Show,’ with Cher starting with ‘The Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour,’ as well as with Joan Rivers, Bette Midler and Lucille Ball, helped shape some of comedy’s most memorable moments on television and stage."

Don Ameche poses with Cher, who wears a Bob Mackie evening gown with a feather headdress. (Bettmann/Bettmann)

Among his most recognizable creations was Cher's dramatic feathered ensemble at the 1986 Academy Awards. His work earned him nine Emmy Awards, a Tony Award for "The Cher Show" and three Academy Award nominations.

"Nobody was allowed to even design a halter dress until Cher started wearing them on Sonny & Cher [in the ‘70s], and then all of a sudden they were in everybody’s collection," Mackie previously told People. "And then girls were showing way more skin than they should have, because Cher was showing more skin than she should have. But she looked good in it."
Dolly Parton wears a Bob Mackie design in 1987. (Jerry Fitzgerald/Getty Images)

His designs – packed with sequins, feathers, beads and a healthy dose of showmanship – made Mackie one of Hollywood's most recognizable costume designers.

Mackie's work has endured for decades as younger stars have chosen to wear his archival work. Sabrina Carpenter has repeatedly dipped into the legendary costume designer’s archives for major appearances.

One of Carpenter’s biggest Mackie moments came at the 2024 MTV Video Music Awards, when she walked the red carpet in a sparkling silver-and-white vintage Mackie gown originally created for Madonna’s 1991 Academy Awards performance.
She paid tribute to Mackie on Instagram, sharing some of the iconic looks she's worn over the past few years.

"Terribly devastated," she wrote on her Instagram story. "I feel so lucky to have met Bob. his one of a kind creations have inspired and brought so much happiness and confidence to my world, and they will continue to always x Mackie girl forever."
Before his death, Mackie acknowledged that younger performers such as Carpenter, Miley Cyrus and Zendaya had developed a new appetite for his archival creations.

title: 'Duck Dynasty' stars weigh in on Lindsay Clancy case, say America is 'turning spiritual issues into diseases'
summary: "Duck Dynasty" stars say the Lindsay Clancy case reveals how America has pathologized spiritual issues and overprescribed antidepressants widely.
story: Jury deliberations begin in the Lindsay Clancy trial as medical experts debate her sanity. Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel breaks down Clancy's history of 32 prescriptions for 13 different psychiatric drugs in the four months leading to the tragedy.
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).
"Duck Dynasty" stars weighed in on a recent court case that captivated America.

During an episode of their podcast, "Unashamed with the Robertson Family," Jase Robertson, Al Robertson and Zach Dasher discussed the Lindsay Clancy case and how it has sparked what they called a "bigger conversation" surrounding "mental health in America."

"I would love to see that conversation emerge because I do think that we have pathologized, and by pathologized, I mean we've turned a lot of spiritual issues into diseases," Dasher said. "We call them like pathologies."

Dasher argued that psychiatric conditions cannot always be measured through laboratory tests, noting, "you can't measure depression with a microscope," and saying that "they don't even know how these antidepressants" and "antipsychotics" work.
Dasher explained that the Lindsay Clancy case shows America is "turning spiritual issues into diseases." ("Unashamed" podcast/YouTube)
‘DUCK DYNASTY' STAR REFUSES TO LET CHILDREN WATCH 'DEBAUCHEROUS' SUPER BOWL HALFTIME SHOWS
Dasher said there is "a biblical answer here" and that a "big discussion" needs to be had.

Clancy recently went on trial on three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her three children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months old. She admitted that she strangled the children before attempting suicide, including by jumping from a second-story window, leaving her paralyzed from the sternum down.

During her trial, which ended in a mistrial after jurors could not reach a unanimous verdict, the defense argued that she should be found not guilty by reason of insanity because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis when she killed the children. Her lawyers also argued that she had been overmedicated while seeking psychiatric treatment.

"I think Granny had a real issue, a lithium deficiency when she was treated with lithium. All of her psychosis subsided," Dasher said, referring to the mother of late family patriarch Phil Robertson. "But man, how many people were just throwing these pills at people?"
Clancy's trial ended in a mistrial after the jury could not come to a unanimous decision. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)

Dasher added that the current mental health system is "not working."

"I think that anybody that is capable of murdering your children... Anyone that does that is obviously in a very sick spiritual state," Dasher said. "There's something going on here that we can't just turn everything into a pathology. Into a disease. Into something that could be treated with a pill."
Dasher maintained, however, that he believes Clancy "should be held accountable and put in a facility," adding that he "does have sympathy in my heart" for her.

Jase agreed with Dasher, saying "some justice has to be there" for the three children, and that "if you kill your three kids, you need to be locked up for the rest of your life."
Jase agreed with Dasher that Clancy needs to be held accountable for her actions. (John Lamparski/Getty Images)

"Two things can be true at the same time. And one is, if somebody murders her children, you have to put that person away," Dasher said. "I mean, they have to. There has to be accountability in that."

He continued: "And yeah, antidepressants are overprescribed. Antipsychotics are probably overprescribed. And so I think both of these things are true at the same time. But I think it's another form of pathologizing what happened to say, ‘Well, the drugs made her do it.’"

title: King Charles draws ‘line in the sand’ with Prince Harry, Meghan Markle after couple caught off guard: expert
summary: King Charles drew a firm line with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle in a letter clarifying their royal status, but Uganda's Invictus Games exit added fuel.
story: King Charles confirms Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not return to royal duties. A letter sent on behalf of the King explains their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and they are now akin to private citizens.
King Charles III has drawn a firm "line in the sand" with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle after sending a letter spelling out their royal standing.

The claim was made by British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex told People magazine they were "surprised" by the timing of a letter circulated by Buckingham Palace clarifying their non-working royal status.

"King Charles' narrative is decisive as he draws a line in the sand — nothing new here, no more discussion required," Chard told Fox News Digital. "I'm sure the Sussexes expected flexibility. Prince Harry may be the king's son, but he lacks power to amend and dictate the monarch's statement."
KING CHARLES III CLARIFIES PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE WILL NOT RESUME ROYAL DUTIES AFTER UK MOVE

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex leave St. Paul's Cathedral after attending the Service of Thanksgiving during Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee celebrations in London in 2022. (Wiktor Szymanowicz/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)

On Sept. 7, a senior palace official reiterated that Harry and Meghan are non-working royals, according to People magazine. The letter, which was issued on behalf of the king, was said to have been shared with the Sussexes. A spokesperson for the couple said they were "a little surprised not to have been told about this in advance," the BBC reported.

Those close to the couple told People magazine they received the letter and, 20 minutes later, sent back some questions. However, they were told that the letter had already been circulated to the media.
The former Prince Charles, with Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex during Trooping the Colour on June 9, 2018, in London. (UK Press via Getty Images)

The letter issued by the Lord Chamberlain, Richard Benyon, Lord Benyon, at the king's direction, pointed out that the couple were "private citizens" and their His and Her Royal Highness styles remain in abeyance and are not used.
WATCH: KING CHARLES CONFIRMS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE WILL NOT RETURN TO ROYAL DUTIES
Chard told Fox News Digital the guidance made one thing clear: they "do not represent the Crown."

"There is no ambiguity about who is in and who is out," she said. "The king is protecting the institution. The public has made it clear they do not want the monarchy to be undermined or damaged by confusion. The letter's statement puts minds at rest."

Prince Harry leaves the High Court in central London on April 8, 2025, after a hearing on the British government's decision to downgrade his personal security during visits to Britain. (Justin Tallis/AFP via Getty Images)

"In part, yes, the monarchy can only have one voice," Chard shared. "Prince William and Princess Catherine are the future king and queen. They officially speak for the crown alongside King Charles and Queen Camilla. It's constitutional, and the crown takes precedence."
Prince William, Prince of Wales, seen here with Catherine, Princess of Wales, is heir to the British throne. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
Royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams said there's another, more silent message the king wants to convey.
"The letter states the palace’s position, but it’s clearly intended as a put-down after the way the royals were blindsided by the Sussexes returning to Britain," he claimed.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle relocated to California in 2020. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"The Sussexes see themselves as public figures, not private citizens," he said. "So, they are ‘surprised,’ but are unlikely to alter their plans. The king was never going to debate anything with the Sussexes. The royals don’t debate, although Queen Elizabeth’s ‘recollections may vary’ is legendary."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Queen Elizabeth II, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry watch a flypast to mark the centenary of the Royal Air Force from the balcony of Buckingham Palace on July 10, 2018, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
The couple relocated to Britain in August ahead of their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, starting school.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family," stated the letter, as quoted by People. "This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected."
Queen Elizabeth II during the wedding of Prince Harry to Meghan Markle on May 19, 2018, in Windsor, England. (Jonathan Brady - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"It follows that there is no change to the current status of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex," it continued. "Their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance and are not used. The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity. In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests."
Prince Harry departs from The Invictus Games Foundation Conversation: From Policy to Practice at Chatham House on July 7, 2026, in London. (Eamonn M. McCormack/Getty Images)
Chard called it a "reality check" for the Sussexes.

"It shouldn’t have been a shock," she said. "The update was inevitable and warranted. Harry and Meghan unexpectedly swanned back to the U.K. and seemingly hoped to continue as if they were still working royals. The blurred lines created an air of confusion, with the majority wondering if Harry was back in the fold of the institution. The petty comment batted back from Team Sussex highlighted bruised egos."
Prince Harry's book "Spare" is displayed in a bookstore on Dec. 16, 2023, in Bath, England. (Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

"Allegedly the Sussexes were caught off guard. The irony when you consider Harry’s book ‘Spare,’ their Netflix documentaries and the Oprah interview catching the British royal family off guard over the years."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Meghan Markle is seen here being interviewed by Oprah Winfrey on March 8, 2021. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

According to People, Harry is preparing to kick off a series of charitable engagements that were planned well ahead of the couple’s return to the U.K. These events will highlight charities and causes he supports, including the Invictus Games. The next iteration of the sporting competition is taking place in 2027 in Birmingham, England.
However, Harry is already facing a rocky arrival.
Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Uganda's chief of defense forces and eldest son of President Yoweri Museveni, on May 13, 2025, in Kampala, Uganda. (Getty Images)
On Sept. 9, Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, the son of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and head of the country's armed forces, announced that his country was withdrawing from the Invictus Games.
Prince Charles and Prince Harry attend the "Our Planet" global premiere at the Natural History Museum in London on April 4, 2019. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"In order not to be construed as being opposed to His Majesty King Charles III of the United Kingdom, whom we deeply revere, Uganda hereby withdraws from the Invictus Games," he wrote on X. "We shall not participate in anything that does not have His Majesty's approval."
Gen. Kainerugaba also told The Times of London, "I have factions in the Ministry of Defence that support that Harry-Meghan nonsense. I had to quash it straight away. I support the monarch. Period."

The Duke of Sussex arrives for an Invictus Games Foundation meeting July 7, 2026, part of the One Year to Go celebrations for the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027. (Stefan Rousseau/PA Images via Getty Images)

A source close to Harry went on to tell People, "They made it very clear that the reason they pulled out was a direct result of perceived guidance from the Lord Chamberlain. This was an unintended or intended consequence of the letter — and that was always going to happen. Hence the wish not to rush it out."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Prince Harry waves as he departs after a visit to the Centre for Blast Injury Studies at Imperial College London on Sept. 10, 2025. (Getty Images)
"The only people suffering as a result are the competitors from Uganda who would have been taking part in next year’s Invictus Games," the insider added.
British royal expert Hilary Fordwich wasn't buying it.

Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attends an Invictus Games Friends and Family reception hosted by the City of The Hague and the Dutch Ministry of Defense at Zuiderpark on April 15, 2022, in The Hague, Netherlands. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Harry blaming this letter for Uganda pulling out of the Invictus Games is a ghastly move on his part," she said. "No doubt Harry and Meghan thought King Charles would accommodate their return or at least consult with them. But their expectations weren't relevant for the royals."

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend the David Foster Foundation 40th Anniversary Celebration on Aug. 7, 2026, in Victoria, British Columbia. (The David Foster Foundation via Getty Images)
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital he believes the letter has caused more harm than good in any peace talks Harry is willing to have with his estranged family.

"My personal opinion on the decision by King Charles to make public a letter conceived by the Lord Chamberlain to reiterate that Harry and Meghan were not working royals was an act of malicious intent initiated by those intending to disrupt their return," he explained.

King Charles III is crowned with St. Edward's Crown by the Archbishop of Canterbury, the Most Rev. Justin Welby, during his coronation ceremony at Westminster Abbey in London, England, on May 6, 2023. (Getty Images)
"The message was unjustified," said Turner. "I hope Harry and Meghan will not rise to the bait and retaliate but calmly move on."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Meghan Markle and Prince Harry attend the wheelchair basketball event during Day 1 of the Invictus Games at the Vancouver Convention Centre in British Columbia, on Feb. 9, 2025. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)

People reported that the king remains supportive of organizations and initiatives, like the Invictus Games, that help wounded service personnel. Palace insiders also pointed out that the letter does not represent a new policy but instead reiterates the terms agreed to at the 2020 "Sandringham Summit" led by the late queen. The family meeting took place shortly before Harry and Meghan stepped back as senior working royals and moved to California.
Royal author Robert Jobson previously told The Daily Mail that "there won't be any war of words" between the king and his younger son.
King Charles, Queen Camilla and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex are seen here in Buckingham Palace in London, on May 22, 2018. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"Perhaps predictably, there was an immediate response from the couple," he told the outlet. "But don’t expect to see anything similar coming from the palace. The king has no intention of being drawn into responding further."
King Charles III and Prince William attend the Thistle Service at St Giles' Cathedral in Edinburgh, Scotland, on July 1, 2026. (Getty Images)

While the Sussexes have returned to the U.K. for an extended stay, they won't resume their roles as working royals. They will live in a private, nonroyal residence outside London while maintaining their California home and a property in Portugal.
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Celine Dion breaks down onstage during emotional return after 6-year hiatus
summary: Celine Dion opened her 26-show Paris residency with tears of joy and a powerful promise fulfilled after six years battling stiff person syndrome.
story: Amy Grant recalls how a chance doctor visit saved her life. The singer was diagnosed with a potentially catastrophic heart condition after  accompanying husband Vince Gill to his cardiologist appointment.
Celine Dion made her return to the stage for the first time in six years while continuing her battle with stiff-person syndrome, and the occasion proved every bit as emotional as anticipated.

The 58-year-old singer — who launched her 26-show residency at the Plenitude Arena in Paris, France, on Sept. 12 - opened the concert with her French-language song "On Ne Change Pas" before tearing up, according to multiple videos circulating online.
"These are, of course, tears of joy. I’m so delighted to see you," Dion told the crowd, according to People.

Celine Dion performs on the opening night of her residency at Paris La Defense Arena on Sept. 12, 2026, in Nanterre, France. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)
Dion later addressed the significance of the performance and her long-awaited return.
"I made a promise to come back, to be back on stage," she said. "So here I am, singing for you and singing for me, singing life!"

The singer also thanked fans for their support and patience during her years away from the stage, telling them, "I am everything I am because you loved me," before performing her hit "Because You Loved Me."

Dion’s career was first interrupted in 2020 when the COVID-19 pandemic forced her to postpone the "Courage World Tour." In January 2022, she canceled the North American leg of the tour, explaining that her recovery from severe muscle spasms was taking longer than expected.

At the time, Dion said she was following the treatment regimen prescribed by her doctors and hoped to return to performing once she regained her health.
Months later, Dion revealed the diagnosis behind her health struggles in an emotional video shared with fans.

"As you know, I've always been an open book. And I wasn't ready to say anything before — but I'm ready now. I've been dealing with problems with my health for a long time. And it's been really difficult for me to face these challenges and talk about everything that I've been going through."
Dion then revealed she had been diagnosed with Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS), which she explained "affects something like one in a million people."

SPS is defined by the Cleveland Clinic as "a rare autoimmune movement disorder that affects the central nervous system (the brain and spinal cord). People with this condition first experience a stiffening of the muscles of their trunk followed, over time, by the development of stiffness and rigidity in the legs and other muscles in the body."
The Canadian singer revealed her stiff-person diagnosis in 2022. (AFP via Getty Images)
Dion explained that the condition sometimes made it difficult for her to walk and prevented her from using her vocal cords "to sing the way I’m used to."

"All I know is singing," Dion said at the time. "It’s what I’ve done all my life. And it’s what I love to do the most."

Dion offered fans a glimpse of her progress in 2024. She received a standing ovation when she appeared at the Grammy Awards to present the album of the year and later documented her health journey in the Prime Video documentary "I Am: Celine Dion."

In July 2024, Dion performed Edith Piaf’s "L’Hymne à l’amour" at the Paris Olympics opening ceremony. The appearance marked her first live performance since revealing her diagnosis and was viewed as a hopeful sign that she could eventually return to concerts.
Celine Dion attends the "I Am: Celine Dion" special screening at Alice Tully Hall in New York City on June 17, 2024. (Getty Images)
Dion’s Paris residency is expected to feature some of her biggest hits, including "My Heart Will Go On," "It’s All Coming Back to Me Now" and "Because You Loved Me."

On Sept. 12 at approximately 9:10 p.m., officers were dispatched to Wild Wing Café in South Carolina after receiving a report of an assault inside the restaurant, according to a statement from the Greenville Police Department obtained by Fox News Digital.
"Upon arrival, officers located several individuals involved in an altercation and detained multiple patrons while the incident was investigated," police said.
HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S BOYFRIEND’S BROTHER REVEALS WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE AIRBNB BEFORE ACTRESS'S DEATH
Hayden Panettiere's boyfriend Brian Hickerson was involved in a bar altercation on Saturday. (Getty Images)
Two of the individuals were identified as Hickerson and his brother, Zachary Hickerson.

Police said Zachary was "highly intoxicated" during the incident and began yelling profanities in a public setting. He was taken into custody on a disorderly conduct charge and transported to the Greenville County Detention Center.
HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S REP SLAMS ‘GOSSIP AND SPECULATION’ AS DEATH INVESTIGATION DEEPENS

In a video circulating online, Hickerson — who was seen handcuffed and bloody outside the restaurant - told Zachary, "GPD leaked it when my girlfriend died," referencing Panettiere's death and the Greenville Police Department.
In another video obtained by TMZ, Hickerson is seen throwing a bar stool before eventually getting carried out of the establishment.
Hickerson was later released from the scene and was not charged, GPD said.
Panettiere was found dead on Aug. 16. (Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images)
HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S MOM DISCLOSES HEARTBREAKING ULTIMATUM IN THEIR FINAL PHONE CALL BEFORE ACTRESS’ DEATH
Representatives for Hickerson and Zachary did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.
The incident comes less than a month after Panettiere, Hickerson’s on-again, off-again girlfriend, was found dead inside a Greenville residence on Aug. 16. She was 36.

Hickerson and his brother, Zach, called 911 after finding the actress unresponsive, according to a police report obtained by Fox News Digital. Hickerson later gave authorities a bag containing medication Panettiere had been taking, according to the report.

The police report claimed Zach appeared "very emotional" while paramedics worked to revive Panettiere. Meanwhile, Hickerson did not become emotional until the "Ice Princess" star was declared deceased.
Officers were also given a bag of medication Panettiere had allegedly been taking by Hickerson.

Hickerson reportedly traveled with the "Remember the Titans" actress from Los Angeles the day before she was found unresponsive at a Greenville, South Carolina, apartment complex on Aug. 16, according to TMZ. The two broke up briefly in 2022, but rekindled their romance the following year. Hickerson's brother confirmed to police Brian was in a relationship with the actress at the time of Panettiere's death.
Hayden Panettiere died at 36 in late August. (Getty Images)

Preliminary autopsy results found no signs of trauma that contributed to Panettiere’s death, the Greenville County Coroner's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital. However, Panettiere's death remains under investigation.
HAYDEN PANETTIERE REMEMBERED BY VIOLA DAVIS, BETHANY JOY LENZ AND OTHER CELEBRITIES AFTER SUDDEN DEATH AT 36
Fox News has learned the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) has also been contacted and is assisting with the investigation.
Shortly after her death, Panettiere's mom, Lesley Vogel, opened up about her daughter's final months during an interview with "Good Morning America."
Panettiere's mom Lesley Vogel spoke about her daughter's struggles days after the star's death. (Getty Images)
One day later, Panettiere's representatives condemned the speculation surrounding Panettiere’s final hours and accused outsiders of turning her death into an opportunity to "fuel gossip."

"Many people who were not close to Hayden are using her death as an opportunity to fuel gossip and speculation about a situation they knew very little about," Panettiere's rep said in a statement shared with US Weekly. "It is deeply disrespectful to her memory and to those who knew and loved her and are actively grieving this tremendous loss."
WLADIMIR KLITSCHKO MOURNS FORMER FIANCÉE HAYDEN PANETTIERE, VOWS TO KEEP HER MEMORY ALIVE FOR DAUGHTER KAYA
"If you have legitimate information that could be helpful, please contact law enforcement rather than turning to social media to speculate publicly about something you do not fully understand."
Panettiere's team also hinted that key details surrounding Panettiere’s death had yet to emerge.

"There is much more to this story than what is currently being discussed publicly, and those closest to Hayden are actively cooperating with the ongoing investigation to help ensure that the truth comes to light and that justice is properly served," the statement concluded.

title: Joanna Gaines reveals why she and Chip walked away from 'Fixer Upper' at the height of its success
summary: Joanna Gaines described a deep "soul weariness" that led her and Chip Gaines to walk away from "Fixer Upper" despite pressure to keep going.
story: HGTV stars Ben and Erin Napier shared their thoughts on the biggest challenges and rewards of working together as a married couple.
Joanna Gaines had success knocking on every door — and she decided to stop answering.
At the height of "Fixer Upper" fame, the home design and lifestyle expert and her husband, Chip Gaines, walked away from the nonstop grind despite pressure from their representatives to keep going.
Years later, Joanna explained that she had reached a point where she was experiencing what she called "soul weariness."
JOANNA GAINES KEEPS LIFE SIMPLE IN TEXAS AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT
Joanna Gaines details why she and Chip walked away from "Fixer Upper." (Christopher Willard / Disney)

"When you start realizing you're living on a thing that's now… the intentionality is gone, and you're just showing up… that doesn't feel fulfilling," she said on the "Joy 101 with Hoda Kotb" podcast. "It actually feels as though we're part of this machine that is like, 'What's the life here?'"

She added, "I would say that was our first pause of like, ‘We're doing all this and seeing great reward … this is wonderful,’ but also never at the expense of … our like livelihood, our happiness, our souls."
That pause would become a blueprint for how Joanna thinks about work — and burnout — today.

"Stopping in that moment was basically us saying … ‘What's worth it is, like are we healthy? Are we good? Is our family good?’ That's the most important thing. So that was really a very pivotal moment for us."
"Fixer Upper" turned Chip and Joanna into television stars, but even as the HGTV hit reached new heights, the couple knew they couldn't keep running at full speed forever.
Joanna Gaines said "Fixer Upper" fame left her with "soul weariness." (Getty Images)

The Gaines’s first stepped in front of television cameras when the "Fixer Upper" pilot aired in 2013. The series followed the husband-and-wife duo as they took on rundown homes in Waco, Texas, and transformed them into polished spaces for their clients — all while growing their increasingly influential Magnolia brand.
The show quickly became a hit, making Joanna and Chip familiar faces far beyond the world of home renovation.
COUNTRY STAR STEPS AWAY FROM MUSIC TO FOCUS ON HIMSELF AFTER FAME TOOK A TOLL
In September 2017, the couple announced they would end "Fixer Upper" after its fifth season, choosing to step away while the series was still riding high.
Joanna said she and Chip have spent almost 25 years building their business. But about three years ago, she said, they stopped seeing where they were headed.
"We stopped seeing vision. We stopped remembering, ‘Like why are we doing this?’"
The couple decided to take the summer off.
KATHIE LEE GIFFORD ADMITS SHE 'WANTED TO DIE' AFTER MISDIAGNOSIS AND MULTIPLE SURGERIES FOR CHRONIC PAIN
However, the decision wasn't consequence-free.
Joanna acknowledged that stepping away meant putting pressure on their team.
"Which meant disappointing our team, disappointing a lot of things … So it cost us something. It cost people something."
"But that three months was time for us to go, ‘We need a break. We need clarity. Why are we building this? What are we doing this for?’"
Joanna remembered the moment she felt the burnout was impossible to ignore.
Chip and Joanna shared how their son leaving for college changed their perspective on parenting. (Photo by Cindy Ord/Getty Images for SiriusXM)
"When you start dreading your days, like ‘I don't want to do that.’"
For Gaines, that sense of dread eventually became so pronounced that she found herself looking for almost any excuse to hit pause — even an unexpected illness.
"You start like wishing for a stomach bug or … 'Okay, maybe back surgery this year would be great.’ Like how do I force myself?" she laughed.
'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD
Physical exhaustion, Joanna explained, is something she knows how to push through.
But the deeper exhaustion is different, she argued.
"So there's that part, but also just … where your soul just feels weary."
She described the "soul" as the deeper part of a person — the place that can run dry even when the body is still capable of performing.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"From a physical standpoint, I can work till I can … I can push past the weariness the physical, but then you get to that layer of like the soul weariness and that's dangerous."
Joanna said that was the warning she is now determined not to ignore, describing the feeling as a "holy fear."
The couple, who created the Magnolia Market empire, has five children. (Nathan Congleton)
For the entrepreneur and television personality who built an empire by constantly creating, the hardest lesson may have been learning that she cannot simply outwork exhaustion.
The Magnolia Network stars tied the knot in 2003. Joanna and Chip are parents to five children — Ella, Drake, Crew, Emmie and Duke.

As the Gaines’s planted their roots in Waco, Texas, their Magnolia businesses took off.
The couple's Magnolia Market at the Silos in Waco pictured. (Getty Images)

After five seasons of "Fixer Upper," the original series ended in 2018. Magnolia Network programming later debuted on Discovery+ in 2021 before the linear Magnolia Network replaced DIY Network in January 2022.

The couple's Magnolia Market at the Silos in Waco includes Magnolia Market, the Shops at the Silos, Silos Baking Co. and Magnolia Press Coffee Co. They also operate Magnolia Table elsewhere in Waco.

The design duo additionally publish "Magnolia Journal" and have written a series of lifestyle books. They have a Magnolia Home furniture and accessories collection, and Joanna created the Hearth & Hand with Magnolia collection for Target.
