title: Accused killers vanish after family massacre before manhunt ends hundreds of miles away
summary: A deadly North Carolina shooting left two dead and two critically injured before suspects Camryn Moore and Cory Armstrong fled across state lines.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A deadly shooting inside a North Carolina family home triggered an urgent search for two accused killers and an interstate manhunt that would end with another burst of gunfire.
Gaston County Police officers responded to a home on Forbes Road at approximately 8:43 a.m. Thursday after receiving a report of gunfire inside the residence.
Officers discovered four people suffering from gunshot wounds. Two were pronounced dead at the scene, while two others were rushed to CaroMont Regional Medical Center with life-threatening injuries.

Police identified the two people killed as Victoria "Heather" Moore, 50, and Megan "Josiah" Bumgardner, 38. The two surviving victims remained in critical but stable condition Friday, according to police.
4 SHOT INSIDE NORTH CAROLINA HOME, 2 KILLED AS POLICE IDENTIFY PERSON OF INTEREST
Gaston County police responded to the Forbes Road home after receiving a report of gunfire inside. (Queen City News)

Detectives identified two residents of the home, Camryn Moore, 26, and Cory Armstrong, 29, as suspects in the bloodshed. WSOC-TV reported that Heather Moore was Camryn Moore’s mother and Bumgardner was her uncle.
Cory Armstrong, 29, was wanted on murder and attempted murder charges following a shooting at a Gaston County home. (Gaston County Police)
Police said they believed everyone involved knew one another and described the shooting as an isolated incident with no continuing threat to the Gaston County community.
Camryn Moore, 26, was accused of killing two people and critically wounding two others inside a North Carolina home. (Gaston County Police)
Investigators have not disclosed what may have triggered the violence.

Camryn Moore and Armstrong allegedly fled Gaston County immediately after the shooting. By Thursday afternoon, detectives had obtained warrants charging each of them with two counts of first-degree murder and two counts of attempted first-degree murder.
WATCH: DEPUTIES HUNT WANTED MAN THROUGH CORNFIELD AFTER HIGH-SPEED CHASE CAUGHT ON CAMERA
Gaston County Police identified two suspects after four people were found shot inside a family home. (Queen City News)

The Gaston County Police Department enlisted the help of the U.S. Marshals Service Carolinas Regional Fugitive Task Force as investigators tracked the pair’s movements across multiple states overnight.
SUSPECTED HUMAN SMUGGLERS LEAD COPS ON 100-MPH CHASE BEFORE BAILING AND ALLEGEDLY COMMITTING ARMED CARJACKING
The search reached Ohio at approximately 8 a.m. Friday, when state troopers spotted the suspects’ vehicle outside Athens and attempted to pull it over, authorities said.
Moore and Armstrong allegedly refused to stop, setting off a multi-county pursuit.

The chase came to a violent end when their vehicle swerved to avoid spike strips deployed in the roadway and crashed, according to information provided to North Carolina investigators by Ohio authorities.
A street view shows the Forbes Road address identified by police in connection with the deadly Gaston County shooting. (Google Maps)
Officers then reported hearing two gunshots coming from the wrecked vehicle.
Law enforcement deployed a drone to look inside and discovered Moore and Armstrong dead. Authorities have not disclosed who fired the shots or officially announced the manner of their deaths.
The Ohio State Highway Patrol is investigating the pursuit, crash and deaths.
Back in Gastonia, neighbors were stunned by the violence that shattered their normally peaceful street.
Loretta Forbes, whose husband’s grandfather built her home in 1914 and gave Forbes Road its name, told WSOC-TV that she knew the family living next door.
"I just kept saying, ‘My God. Oh God,’ coming down the stairs," Forbes told the outlet. "They seem to be very nice people. It just shakes you up to think that could happen so close by."
Forbes said she was praying for the family and searching for answers.
"I want to know what’s happened," she said. "I want to know about the family."
Jennifer Greene, a friend and co-worker of Heather Moore, drove to the home after Moore unexpectedly failed to report for her shift.
SUSPECTED DUI DRIVER LEADS COPS ON WILD CHASE BEFORE DRAMATIC TAKEDOWN ON POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH
Friends remembered Victoria "Heather" Moore as a warm and loving person after she was killed in the Gaston County shooting. (Heather Moore Facebook)
"This was a tragic act of violence that resulted in the loss of multiple lives and left others critically injured," the Gaston County Police Department said.
"Although the search for the suspects has ended, our investigation has not," police added.
Heather Moore, left, was remembered by friends as a loving woman who brought warmth into every room. (GoFundMe)

Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact Detective G. Lancaster at 704-866-3320 or CrimeStoppers at 704-861-8000.

title: Charlie Kirk statue defaced with red paint, Jesus crossed out days after 1-year mark of assassination
summary: Red paint was smeared across the Charlie Kirk statue at Turning Point USA's Phoenix headquarters, with a Christian tribute defaced days after unveiling.
story: President Donald Trump honors Charlie Kirk during a speech at the RNC midterm convention. 'The Five' co-hosts reflect on Kirk's legacy, his impact through Turning Point USA, and the expansion of the group to more than 3,500 high school clubs one year after his assassination.

Vandals smeared bright red paint across a newly unveiled statue of Charlie Kirk and defaced a Christian tribute outside Turning Point USA’s Phoenix headquarters early Sunday, just three days after the memorial was installed.
Images from the headquarters show red paint streaked across the eight-foot statue’s face and neck, with a crude frowning face drawn across its chest.

A sign at the base of the statue bearing Kirk’s image and the words "Jesus defeated death so you can live" was also targeted. The word "Jesus" and an image of a cross appeared to be crossed out, while "Satan" was apparently scrawled across the display.
REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR
Kirk's widow, Erika, who now serves as Turning Point USA CEO, responded with a defiant vow to rebuild, saying the vandals would not erase her husband’s legacy or silence Christians.
"Charlie once said we should be building two statues for every statue that they tear down," Erika Kirk wrote, adding that her husband’s instinct was always to create rather than destroy.

She said the bullet that killed her husband only amplified his voice and predicted the spray paint would spread his legacy even further. She also vowed to restore the statue, replace Jesus Christ’s name on the damaged sign and continue the movement her husband built.
"God will not be mocked," Erika Kirk wrote.
Phoenix police confirmed to Fox News Digital that the department began receiving calls around 8:09 a.m. reporting vandalism to a memorial in the area of 4900 East Beverly Road.
"Officers have responded to the location, and the incident is under investigation," police said.
No arrests or suspect descriptions had been announced as of Sunday afternoon.

"This morning we woke up to radical criminals vandalizing our headquarters," Turning Point USA Chief Operating Officer Tyler Bowyer wrote on social media. "Crossing over Charlie’s face, scratching out Jesus and the Cross and spraying red paint on his neck.
"This isn’t the country we want to live in," Bowyer added. "Arizona is not Gotham."
INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES
Bowyer, who went to the headquarters as police investigated, said TPUSA was prepared to clean the memorial as soon as authorities released the scene.
"God bless the police as they investigate the violent thugs who did this," Bowyer wrote.
TPUSA also released video showing the damage and encouraged its supporters to vote ahead of the midterm elections.
"Hate cannot win," the organization wrote. "The radical Left is showing up to vote. What are you doing to save the country from this?"
In a follow-up statement, TPUSA said it would restore the statue and replace the damaged signs while reviewing footage of the incident and working with law enforcement to identify those responsible.
"Vandalism like this is not funny, it’s diabolical," the organization wrote. "The incident happened in the middle of the night because evil never sleeps."
TPUSA said the vandals went beyond spraying Kirk’s face and neck with red paint, accusing them of making an "intentional decision" to cross out Jesus’ name on the nearby sign.
The organization ended its response by quoting John 15:18: "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first."
Later Sunday, TPUSA spokesman Andrew Kolvet announced that the statue had been restored.
"The team rallied and got the statue back looking good as new," Kolvet wrote. "Evil may never sleep, but neither do we."
"We won’t stop. We will win. They will lose," he added.
The vandalism struck only days after TPUSA unveiled the bronze statue Thursday to mark one year since Kirk was assassinated while speaking at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025.
CHARLIE KIRK STATUE BOUND FOR NY'S TIMES SQUARE AS SCULPTOR DEFIES THREATS AHEAD OF UNVEILING
A person visits the makeshift memorial for Charlie Kirk outside the headquarters of Turning Point USA on September 18, 2025, in Phoenix, Arizona. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
The statue depicts Kirk wearing his signature "Freedom" T-shirt and cross necklace. Those who knew him said the sculpture captured details down to his wedding ring, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

Turning Point USA commissioned Utah artist Quintin McCann to create the memorial after he began working on a portrait of Kirk the evening the conservative activist was killed, according to the outlet.
ITALIAN ARTIST UNVEILS CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL STATUE HE PLANS TO FEATURE AT TIMES SQUARE

"Someone’s death, who I’ve never met, has never impacted me so much," McCann told FOX 10. "And I’m sure many people can agree. And I just stayed at work that evening and just started sculpting his portrait."
The statue was initially placed outside TPUSA’s headquarters near 48th Street and Beverly Road but was expected to be moved indoors for security reasons by the end of the week, the outlet reported.
REPUBLICAN CONVENTION ATTENDEES SHARE HEARTFELT TRIBUTES TO LATE CHARLIE KIRK ON ASSASSINATION ANNIVERSARY
Conservative voices erupted over the attack, condemning the vandalism as another assault on Kirk’s family, friends and legacy.
"Truly abhorrent," Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., wrote on X. "The Charlie Kirk statue that was just unveiled at Turning Point’s HQ was vandalized overnight with red paint.

"The young people who work at Turning Point don’t deserve this, Charlie’s family doesn’t deserve this, his friends don’t deserve this," Hamadeh added. "The left is intolerant and militant. Evil exists and must be confronted continuously."
Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., was equally blunt.
"This is absolute evil," Biggs wrote.
Conservative commentator Benny Johnson accused the vandals of trying to intimidate Kirk’s supporters.
"These people are incapable of building anything, all they know is destruction," Johnson wrote. "Keep these demons out of power."
TPUSA contributor Alex Clark said seeing the damage brought her to tears before issuing a dire warning to conservative voters.
"The left wants to tap dance in your blood and throw confetti at your gravestone," Clark wrote. "Vote red in midterms like your life depends on it because it actually does as a conservative."

Turning Point USA Chief of Staff Mikey McCoy urged conservatives to answer the vandalism with faith, invoking Kirk’s willingness to return to hostile campuses and the biblical examples of Stephen and Christ praying for those who persecuted them.

"Then I can surrender all the anger, and pure disgust that I feel at seeing this to a just and holy God," McCoy wrote, saying he would pray instead for the repentance and salvation of those responsible.
"Lord, help our Country," he added. "Open their eyes. Break their hearts. Save them."

Bowyer also blasted Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs, accusing her of failing to pursue bipartisanship after Kirk’s killing and pointing to her veto of legislation that would have named Loop 202 in Kirk’s honor.

Hobbs said in her March veto letter that she condemned political violence but argued highway-naming decisions should remain nonpartisan and be handled by the state board responsible for such designations.

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking on his American Comeback Tour when he was shot and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
Kirk was 31 when he was shot and killed during a TPUSA event at Utah Valley University.
Tyler Robinson, 23, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges in Kirk’s death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

Erika Kirk took over as CEO of Turning Point USA after her husband’s assassination. The conservative organization he co-founded in 2012 has continued expanding its network of high school and college chapters since his death.

title: Arrest rips apart media narrative on death of Black woman found hanging from Mississippi tree
summary: Jarques Ratliff faces a murder charge in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother found hanging from a tree behind a Jackson, Mississippi home.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Mississippi authorities have arrested a 51-year-old man on a murder charge after an official homicide ruling in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black mother of four found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned home last month.

The arrest follows weeks of intense media attention and widespread online discussion regarding the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s death in a state with a historic legacy of racialized violence. But law enforcement officials confirmed that the suspect taken into custody is Jarques Ratliff, a Black Jackson resident who had a prior personal connection with Fortune.

Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney announced during a news conference Saturday that Ratliff was taken into custody without incident while walking along Capitol Street in Jackson, shortly after officers executed search warrants at related properties.
AOC’S ‘MODERN-DAY LYNCHINGS’ CLAIM TORN TO SHREDS ONLINE AS BLACK HANGING CASE FINDINGS TELL A DIFFERENT STORY

Chief Brackney emphasized that while the arrest marks a significant breakthrough, the investigation remains active and additional arrest warrants are expected to be served as detectives follow further leads.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., last week warned of "racial terror" and "widespread modern-day lynchings" in the U.S. as she joined dozens of Democrats demanding that the Department of Justice investigate hanging deaths of Black Americans.
Christy Spivey poses with a portrait of her late daughter Tasia Fortune Sept. 8, 2026, in Marion, Ky. (AP Photo/George Walker IV)
Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson.

Although investigators logged hundreds of hours interviewing nearly 15 individuals and reviewing physical evidence over the past month, formal arrest warrants could not be executed until the Mississippi State Medical Examiner’s Office officially classified Fortune’s death a homicide late Thursday.

Once that classification was handed down, members of the Jackson Police Department's robbery-homicide unit moved swiftly to secure and execute two search warrants alongside the arrest warrant for Ratliff.

Addressing public interest in the case, Chief Brackney acknowledged the heightened scrutiny but stressed that law enforcement remains strictly guided by verifiable physical evidence rather than external speculation. She noted that authorities understood public concern given Mississippi's history but said the department is bound to ensure all public statements are backed by forensic facts.
Tasia Fortune in a portrait displayed Sept. 8, 2026, in Marion, Ky. Inset: Jarques Ratliff, who was arrested in connection to Fortune's death. (AP Photo/George Walker IV; Jackson Police Department)

"We understand that this case has received media attention from across the globe and across the community. We understand the questions and the desire for answers given Mississippi's history," Brackney said.

"We understand this case is being viewed through a broader lens — a global lens — and we do not dismiss those concerns. We are taking them seriously. At the same time, we do have a responsibility to make sure that what we say publicly is supported by our evidence and the facts."

Brackney also directly clarified that law enforcement had never officially designated any persons of interest prior to Ratliff’s arrest, refuting social media reports that a 65-year-old man had previously been identified as a suspect.
Jackson Police Chief RaShall Brackney speaking at a news conference. (Jackson Police Department)
COPS DROP MURDER PROBE AFTER CORONER RULES MAN’S BLOODY STABBING DEATH WAS FREAK ACCIDENT

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, said police promptly notified her family of the homicide ruling and Ratliff's arrest on Friday. Spivey expressed gratitude for the police work and reiterated her firm belief that her daughter did not die by suicide, adding that Fortune would never take her own life.
Police say Fortune’s body was discovered Aug. 3 in the backyard of a vacant property in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in Jackson. (Google Maps)

According to family members and an online obituary published in Kentucky, Fortune grew up in Kentucky, skipped her junior year of high school and was a star cross-country runner guided by strong religious faith before relocating to Jackson a decade ago.
Spivey noted that her daughter had experienced homelessness in recent years but was actively working to launch a cleaning business and stabilize her life prior to her death.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Ratliff is being held at the Hinds County Detention Center on a charge of murder. According to Mississippi State Defender André de Gruy, Ratliff is scheduled to make his initial appearance in Jackson Municipal Court no later than Monday morning, where formal charges will be read and bond conditions set.

Police have not publicly detailed the specific physical evidence linking Ratliff to the scene, nor have they expanded on the exact nature of his personal association with Fortune as investigators prepare for further potential arrests.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: Female passenger undresses on American Airlines flight, engages in 'indecent acts,' crew reports
summary: A female passenger on American Airlines Flight 1779 reportedly undressed and performed indecent acts mid-flight, prompting law enforcement at Miami.

Law enforcement officers met an American Airlines flight upon its arrival at Miami International Airport late Friday night following reports of a female passenger undressing and behaving indecently mid-flight.

The flight landed in Miami at approximately 11:23 p.m. EDT.
As the Airbus A319 was en route to Florida, flight attendants alerted the cockpit crew to a disturbance involving a passenger in row 9.
UNRULY PASSENGERS COULD BE BANNED FOR LIFE FROM MULTIPLE AIRLINES UNDER NEW PROPOSAL
An American Airlines jet at Miami International Airport averting a near tragedy Friday night. (Ronen Tivony/NurPhoto)

An American Airlines flight after landing at Chicago O'Hare International Airport on Aug. 17. (Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT

An American Airlines Boeing 737-800 sits at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport in Dallas, Texas, on Nov. 23, 2017. (Getty Images)

title: Georgia killer who murdered two suburban real estate agents faces execution after 23-year wait for justice
summary: Lori Brown's mother recalls the 2003 Powder Springs murders of two real estate agents as Stacey Ian Humphreys' Georgia execution date nears.
story: Internet searches from conman Brian Walshe and voicemails from his mother, Diana, take center stage in a new Fox Nation special on the Ana Walshe murder case.

As the execution date nears for a Georgia man convicted of killing two real estate agents, the mother of one victim is remembering the women who were murdered while simply doing their jobs and the risks that real estate professionals still face.
Barring a last-minute judicial stay or executive clemency, Stacey Ian Humphreys, 53, is scheduled for execution Sept. 16 at the Georgia Diagnostic and Classification Prison in Jackson.

On Nov. 3, 2003, Lori Brown, 21, and Cynthia "Cyndi" Williams, 33, were working from a model home office inside the Oakwind subdivision, a rapidly growing, upscale residential development in Powder Springs, when Humphreys fatally shot them.
The office welcomed prospective buyers, making interactions with unfamiliar visitors a routine part of their professions.
74-YEAR-OLD BECOMES FLORIDA'S OLDEST INMATE EXECUTED AFTER 1982 KILLING OF TEEN
Cyndi Williams and Lori Brown (Cobb County Superior Court)
Williams returned to the office after lunch and encountered Humphreys first. Brown arrived shortly afterward and unknowingly walked into an armed robbery already underway.
Humphreys held the women at gunpoint, made them strip and killed them before fleeing with their ATM cards. There was no evidence of sexual assault.

Ed Greathouse, a retired supervisory investigator with the Cobb County Judicial Circuit who assisted the prosecution, told Fox News Digital that investigators never determined why Humphreys chose that particular office over others in the development.
A natural in real estate
For Brown's mother, longtime real estate agent Linda Brown, her daughter’s outgoing personality made her a perfect fit for the profession.
"Let me tell you, she was a rascal growing up," Linda told Fox News Digital. "She had a gregarious spirit about her.
"She was a people person from the time she was small. She never met a stranger. That's why real estate was such a perfect place for her, because she was really good at it."

Brown formed a close friendship with Williams, who took Brown under her wing. She also planned to marry her high school sweetheart in 2004. She had been tasting wedding cakes and looking at venues, Linda said.
On the day she was killed, her wedding planning notebook sat neatly on her office desk.
"Sometimes I think it's my fault. I should have never let her go in this direction with real estate, but, you know, she was going to do what she was going to do," Linda added.
Stacey Humphreys was convicted of murder. (Georgia Department of Corrections)
Arrest and conviction
After the murders, Humphreys used the stolen bank cards to withdraw over $3,000, according to court records.

On Nov. 8, 2003, authorities arrested Humphreys in a rental Jeep Grand Cherokee after a high-speed chase in Wisconsin. Investigators found the murder weapon inside the rental, along with Williams' blood on the gun. They found Brown's blood inside Humphreys’ personal vehicle, according to the Georgia Supreme Court record.
Greathouse said investigators believed Humphreys was heading toward Canada when a Waukesha County officer apprehended him.

"It was fairly common knowledge in prison, where he had been, and certainly in law enforcement, that if you get to Canada, Canada won't extradite you back to the United States unless the prosecutor absolutely will not pursue the death penalty," he said.

Although Humphreys insisted he did not remember killing the women, he told investigators, "I know I did it. I know it just as well as I know my own name."
Authorities learned that Humphreys was behind on his vehicle payments and had taken out a high-interest payday loan he could not afford.

In 2007, a Glynn County jury convicted Humphreys of two counts of malice murder, along with armed robbery, kidnapping and aggravated assault. He pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.
THREE DEATH ROW INMATES EXECUTED BY LETHAL INJECTION IN RARE SAME-DAY STRING ACROSS US
Linda Brown remains skeptical that Humphreys' execution will take place after 23 years. (Linda Brown)
In favor of the death penalty
The state scheduled Humphreys' execution for Dec. 17, 2025, but the State Board of Pardons and Paroles postponed the date and his clemency hearing amid legal challenges.
Greathouse said obtaining a death sentence was unusual during his years working capital cases in Cobb County.

"I did 13 death penalty cases in Cobb County during my tenure, and that was, I think, one of two we actually achieved the death penalty," he said. "It's really rare."

Nearly 23 years after her daughter’s death, Linda remains skeptical that Humphreys' execution will take place.

"Not only did we lose these two girls, but we had to go through 4½ years waiting for a trial to come to an end. So, here we are 23 years later," she said. "I’m still in favor of the death penalty for this man that took their lives."
Humphreys' attorney filed a motion this past week to try to throw out his death sentence over claims of jury misconduct, but a judge rejected that motion on Thursday, FOX 5 Atlanta reported.

title: Man accused in brutal motel stabbing sought as person of interest in 4 deaths, child attack
summary: Kaegan Jude Solet is sought as a person of interest after four people were found stabbed to death and a child critically wounded in Houma, Louisiana.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Louisiana man previously accused of repeatedly stabbing a woman and locking her inside a motel room is now being sought by law enforcement after four people were found stabbed to death and a child was critically wounded.

Terrebonne Parish Sheriff Tim Soignet said detectives identified 47-year-old Houma resident Kaegan Jude Solet as a person of interest in the apparent series of stabbing incidents in the Ashland Drive area of Houma.
Deputies were initially called to the 200 block of Ashland Drive, where they discovered the wounded child, according to the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office.
NORTH CAROLINA MAN BROKE INTO EX'S HOME, FATALLY STABBED HIS 5-YEAR-OLD SON BEFORE GOING TO TACO BELL: POLICE

The Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office identified Kaegan Jude Solet as a person of interest. Anyone with information about his whereabouts is urged to contact detectives. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)

The child was flown to an out-of-area hospital and remained in critical but stable condition after suffering "extremely significant" injuries, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office Lt. Blake Tabor told Fox News Digital.
"That’s not something that you want to see ever," Tabor said.
TWO TEEN SUSPECTS HELD AFTER 5 FAMILY MEMBERS KILLED IN 'TARGETED MASS SHOOTING'
Deputies found four people dead inside homes near Ashland Drive after responding to a critically wounded child, authorities said. (Google Maps)
As deputies searched the surrounding area, they made a grim discovery inside nearby homes.

At least four victims were found dead, according to the sheriff’s office. Authorities have not released their identities or disclosed what relationship, if any, they had to one another, the injured child or Solet.
SUSPECT ARRESTED AFTER MOM, PREGNANT TEEN, 12-YEAR-OLD FOUND BOUND AND MURDERED
Investigators also have not said what may have sparked the violence or whether the victims were attacked inside more than one home.
Solet has not been arrested or charged in the latest deaths. The sheriff’s office stressed that identifying him as a person of interest does not mean he has been accused of a crime.
DEPUTY US MARSHAL FATALLY SHOT WHILE SERVING ARREST WARRANT IN LOUISIANA
Authorities believe Solet is likely still in the area but said they are not ruling out other possibilities.
"We’re using every investigative tool that we have," Tabor said. "Our hope is that we plan to get him in custody very quickly."
Tabor said investigators do not have information indicating Solet intends to leave the state or "go on the run" but added that authorities are "exploring all options."
Solet had not been located as of the latest update.
REPEAT OFFENDER RELEASED EARLY FROM JAIL NOW CHARGED WITH CAPITAL MURDER OF PREGNANT WOMAN
Authorities are searching for Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, after identifying him as a person of interest in a series of deadly stabbing incidents. (Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office)
The latest investigation is not the first time Solet’s name has surfaced in violent crime allegations.
Solet was arrested in December 2019 after allegedly stabbing a woman repeatedly and leaving her locked inside a Houma motel room, according to a police news release from the time.
Houma police responded to the Red Carpet Inn shortly after midnight on Christmas Eve 2019 and found a 59-year-old woman lying on the floor of her room with numerous stab wounds.
The Red Carpet Inn in Houma, La., where Kaegan Solet allegedly stabbed a woman in 2019. (Google Maps)
The woman was taken by ambulance to a medical facility with injuries considered life-threatening, police said.
Witnesses told investigators they heard someone yelling for help from inside the room. When they entered, they found the woman on the floor and unable to move.
Investigators identified Solet, then 40, as the suspect and said he had been invited into the woman’s room before the two became involved in an argument.

Police alleged the confrontation turned physical, and Solet repeatedly stabbed the woman in her head and upper body. He then allegedly fled and locked the motel room door behind him, leaving the critically wounded woman inside.
MANIAC WHO STABBED BOY OUTSIDE WALMART WAS PREVIOUSLY FREED AFTER ATTACKING DAD, CHURCH RAMPAGE: REPORT
Kaegan Jude Solet had not been arrested or charged in the latest deaths as authorities continued searching for him. (Houma Police Department)
Officers located Solet approximately 18 hours later and took him into custody without incident.
He was transported to the Terrebonne Parish Criminal Justice Complex and booked on one count of attempted second-degree murder, according to Houma police.
Terrebonne Parish detectives had also obtained a warrant for Solet’s arrest on a charge of second-degree murder in January 2019, according to a separate sheriff’s office news release.

The warrant was obtained during the investigation into the Jan. 9, 2019, killing of Kemple Paul Scott Lovell. Then-Sheriff Jerry Larpenter said detectives were searching for Solet, who had last been seen in the Houma area.
The final dispositions of both 2019 cases were not immediately available.
ILLINOIS NO-CASH BAIL LAW 'UTTERLY MANIPULATED' BY VIOLENT OFFENDERS, DEM ALDERMAN SAYS AFTER COP'S KILLING
Asked why Solet was no longer in custody, Tabor said authorities were also searching for answers.
"I can’t tell you. Certainly, that’s the hot question, right? Why is he out?" Tabor said. "We’re probably just as stunned as everyone else is."

Tabor emphasized that the sheriff’s office has a strong working relationship with the Terrebonne Parish District Attorney’s Office but said questions remain about how Solet’s previous cases were handled.
"How this slipped through, I certainly don’t know, but it’s a question that probably needs to be answered," Tabor said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the district attorney’s office seeking the circumstances surrounding Solet’s release and whether he remained under any court-ordered supervision but did not immediately receive a response.
Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and develop information surrounding the latest deadly incidents as the search for Solet continues.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The sheriff’s office urged anyone with information about his whereabouts to contact Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Office detectives at 985-876-2500.
The investigation remains active and in its preliminary stages. Authorities said additional details will be released as they become available.

title: Florida woman accused of setting stranger on fire at gas station, leaving horrific burns

story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Florida woman pumping gas was engulfed in a fireball after a stranger allegedly walked up and deliberately ignited the fuel with a lighter in a seemingly random attack, police said.

The 41-year-old victim, identified in court records as Christine Sherbuk, was filling her Volvo SUV at a Mobil gas station in St. Petersburg on Thursday night when Eleanor Crawford approached her, according to police and an arrest affidavit.
Crawford, 41, allegedly lit the gasoline at about 8 p.m., setting the SUV ablaze and leaving Sherbuk with second-degree burns to her arms and back.
GEORGIA MOTHER FIGHTS OFF ALLEGED CHILD SNATCHER WITH GAS PUMP IN SURVEILLANCE VIDEO
Eleanor Crawford allegedly ignited gasoline while a woman fueled her SUV at a St. Petersburg Mobil station, leaving the victim seriously burned, police said. (St. Petersburg Police Department)
She was rushed to the trauma center at Tampa General Hospital in serious condition. Police said she was stabilized and is expected to survive.
Scotty Gramling told Fox 13 Tampa Bay he was parked nearby when the violence erupted and raced to help Sherbuk as flames swallowed her vehicle.
MAN ARRESTED AFTER ALLEGEDLY THROWING MOLOTOV COCKTAIL AT PERSON IN WHEELCHAIR NEAR OKC POLICE HEADQUARTERS
Police said a woman suffered second-degree burns after a stranger allegedly ignited gasoline as she fueled her SUV at this St. Petersburg Mobil station. (Fox 13 Tampa Bay)
Gramling helped the injured woman into his truck and called 911. He described what he witnessed as a "fireball."

Moments earlier, Gramling said, he had called the police non-emergency line after seeing Crawford involved in some kind of altercation across the street. It appeared someone was trying to pull her out of the roadway before a fight broke out, he told the outlet.
Officers were already heading to that disturbance when the gas station attack unfolded, according to the outlet.
Police caught Crawford a couple of blocks away within about 20 minutes. The arrest affidavit says multiple witnesses saw her ignite the gasoline and that the incident was captured on video.
SUSPECT NAMED IN NEW YORK CITY ALLEGED INCENDIARY DEVICE ATTACK, HAD 'ANTI-ICE STUFF' ON HIM
St. Petersburg police arrested Eleanor Crawford shortly after a woman was seriously burned in an alleged gas station arson attack. (St. Petersburg Police Department)
Crawford and Sherbuk did not know each other, investigators said. Authorities have not identified a motive.

"I don't know if alcohol and drugs were involved, but indicative of her history, there might've been something that diminished capacity there," Assistant Police Chief Mike Kovacsev told Fox 13. "Why would she even do something like this?"
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH ABUSING HER KIDS, SETTING FIRE IN HOUSE WHILE MAKING MENTAL HEALTH DEFENSE
Police said Crawford has an extensive record that includes several drug- and alcohol-related charges. Authorities have not said whether she was under the influence at the time of the alleged attack.

"It's kind of a unique case because you don't see anything like this, especially something that results in such horrific burns," Kovacsev said. "But they went out there, they worked with the fire department and, luckily, they were able to get her stabilized, and she's going to make it."
ARMY VETERAN FACES ARSON CHARGE AFTER ATTACK OUTSIDE NYC FEDERAL BUILDING: 'CAME ARMED WITH BAD INTENTIONS'
Police units respond to an emergency. (Getty Images)
Crawford was charged with attempted felony murder and two counts of arson. She is being held on $350,000 bond while awaiting trial.
A judge ordered her to be fitted with a GPS monitor by the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office before her release from jail, court records show.

title: Son of notorious Somali dictator reportedly living in Ohio, decades after brutal regime's collapse
summary: Ayanle Siad Barre, son of Somalia's former dictator, has been living in Ohio's large Somali community, prompting calls for a U.S. investigation.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

The son of former Somali dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, whose brutal regime was accused of widespread atrocities during his more than two decades in power, has been living in Ohio for years, according to a new report.
Ayanle Siad Barre, 61, lives in the Columbus area, home to a large Somali community, the New York Post reported. The outlet also identified his sister, Deka Mohamed Siad, as living in Ohio.

Their father ruled Somalia from 1969, until his government was overthrown in 1991. His regime has been accused of mass killings that left as many as 200,000 people dead, torture and other human rights abuses, including atrocities against the Isaaq clan. Mohamed Siad Barre died in 1995.

Historian and Oxford University doctoral researcher Mohamed Haji Ingiriis described Ayanle as his father's "right-hand man" and alleged that he wielded significant power within the government, according to the Post. Fox News Digital has not independently verified those allegations.
TRUMP DOJ ESCALATES CITIZENSHIP CRACKDOWN ON GROUP ACCUSED OF HIDING TERROR TIES, VIOLENT CRIMES
Mohamed Siad Barre, president of Somalia, on Nov. 18, 1981 (UPI/Bettmann Archive/Getty Images, File)
Fox News Digital previously reported that another figure from the Barre era, former Somali military commander Yusuf Abdi Ali, had lived in the U.S. before being deported.

An immigration judge determined in 2024 that Ali personally engaged in torture while serving in the Somali National Army and ordered soldiers under his command to detain and torture civilians and assist in extrajudicial killings, according to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Ali, who had been living as a permanent resident in Virginia, was deported to Somalia in December 2024.
"The United States will not be a safe haven for those who commit human rights violations," ICE official Russell Hott said at the time.
EX-PHILIPPINE PRESIDENT DUTERTE TO FACE TRIAL ON CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY CHARGES
Somalia President Mohamad Siad Barre in 1981. (Kevin Fleming/Corbis via Getty Images, File)
The Post also reported that Ayanle established a translation services company called Somal Global Services.
His sister, Deka, and her late husband operated Vanguard Home Health Care, which received more than $1.8 million in Medicare funding, according to documents reviewed by the publication.
The Post reported that the company appeared to have operated legitimately and filed the appropriate paperwork.
Some survivors of the Barre regime are now calling for U.S. authorities to investigate members of the former dictator's family.
Human rights activist Suleiman Bolaleh called for an investigation to determine what Barre family members knew or did during the dictatorship, according to the Post.
DOJ CHARGES 19 DEFENDANTS IN ALLEGED $4M PHILADELPHIA MEDICARE AND MEDICAID FRAUD

Mohamed Siad Barre, left, president of the Somali Democratic Republic from 1969 to 1991, stands with military officers and senior regime officials in Mogadishu in 1969. (Pictures from History/Universal, File)
The calls for an investigation do not establish wrongdoing by Ayanle or other family members.
Fox News Digital reached out to Ayanle Siad Barre for comment, but attempts to reach him through publicly listed contact information were unsuccessful.

ICE, the Department of Justice and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

title: NATO jets shoot down drone in Lithuanian airspace as Russia grows 'increasingly reckless,' Rutte says
summary: Two Italian Eurofighter Typhoons scrambled under NATO command and downed a drone over Lithuania that officials say likely came from Belarus.
story: Two Italian Eurofighters scrambled under NATO command to intercept an explosive-laden drone over Lithuania, marking the nation's first operational air defense shootdown. (Lithuanian Army)

Two Italian Eurofighter Typhoons operating under NATO command scrambled overnight and shot down a drone over Lithuania, marking the first time a drone has been downed in the Baltic nation's airspace, officials said Tuesday.
The incident came less than a day after NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned that strikes close to alliance territory would drive the 32-nation bloc to increase its support for Ukraine.
The drone was destroyed near the village of Pratkūnai, about 60 miles northwest of the capital, Vilnius.
RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS

Lithuanian soldiers are securing the area where Italian fighter jets during NATO's Baltic Air Policing Mission shot down a drone early morning near Pratkunai village, Kaisiadorys district roughly 60 miles northwest of the capital Vilnius, Lithuania, Tuesday, Sept. 15, 2026.

"Last night, two Italian Eurofighters deployed on NATO Air Defence mission at Siauliai, scrambled and shot down a drone over Lithuanian airspace," a NATO official told Fox News Digital. "The operation was coordinated through NATO’s Combined Air Operations Centre in Uedem, Germany. Investigations are ongoing together with national authorities."
Lithuanian officials said the drone most likely entered from neighboring Belarus and remained in the country's airspace for about 30 minutes before it was intercepted.
Lithuanian soldiers are securing the area where Italian fighter jets during NATO's Baltic Air Policing Mission shot down a drone early this morning near Pratkunai village. (AP Photo)
Lithuanian Air Force Commander Antanas Matutis said the recovered drone was "likely" carrying explosives.
Authorities are examining the wreckage of the downed drone to determine its origin and purpose.
The incident comes amid heightened tensions along NATO's eastern flank.
RUSSIA EXPOSES NATO WEAPONS GAP AS TOP COMMANDER WARNS ‘THE MATH IS NOT IN FAVOR OF THE WEST’
Speaking in Brussels on Monday, Rutte said strikes "close to NATO territory" showed Russian President Vladimir Putin's "desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror."
"Russia is growing increasingly reckless as it continues its terrible war against Ukraine," Rutte said, while pledging to strengthen NATO defenses along its eastern flank.

Debris of what, according to the Lithuanian national crisis management centre, was a drone shot down by a NATO fighter jet, lies on the ground near Pratkunai village, Lithuania, September 15, 2026, in this screengrab from a handout video. (Lithuanian Army/Handout via Reuters)

In a separate incident Tuesday, Denmark said a Russian frigate fired flares toward a Danish military helicopter conducting routine surveillance over the Baltic Sea. Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador over the encounter.
Meanwhile, Russia continued drone strikes across Ukraine, killing three people in Kyiv, Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, according to Ukrainian officials.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv remained ready to support de-escalation if the U.S. could ensure Russia was prepared to stop its attacks. Ukrainian forces also struck an oil refinery in Syzran and targeted a drone production facility in Taganrog, he said.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: UK breakup push escalates amid historic pact after Trump backs reunification of Ireland
summary: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland leaders signed a historic joint declaration in Cardiff, warning that Westminster's time is coming to an end.
story: President Donald Trump expressed support for Irish unification during a meeting in Dublin, just days after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham ruled out potential referendums in Northern Ireland and Scotland.

The leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland called Monday for the British government to "prepare for, plan and facilitate" constitutional change that could lead to the breakup of the United Kingdom, with the remarks coming days after President Donald Trump said he would "love to see" Irish reunification.

"Westminster’s time is coming to an end," Scottish First Minister John Swinney, Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O’Neill said in a historic joint declaration issued in Cardiff.
The nationalist party leaders had met Monday to strengthen cooperation among Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland and advance what they described as "constitutional change."
KEIR STARMER REPORTEDLY CONSIDERING STEPPING DOWN AS PM AND COULD ANNOUNCE TIMETABLE FOR DEPARTURE
Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish leaders say that Westminster is not working and are back self-determination. (Adrian DENNIS / AFP via Getty Images)
The declaration, signed during the summit in Cardiff, signals an unprecedented challenge to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the U.K.’s constitutional settlement.
Trump spoke about the status of Northern Ireland over the weekend, saying Saturday during a visit to Dublin: "It’s going to happen eventually. It might as well happen now."
On Sunday, Trump repeated his support for a united Ireland, saying it made sense to merge the Republic of Ireland with Northern Ireland.
"It just seems to me that you have Northern Ireland and you have Ireland, and it would seem to me that one of the naturals of all time is put them together," Trump said in Doonbeg.
NIGEL FARAGE RESIGNING FROM UK PARLIAMENT
President Donald Trump reacts on the first tee during the final day of the Irish Open on Sept. 13, 2026, in Doonbeg, Ireland. (Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)
"You asked about Scotland. That one I won't talk about yet. I'll save that for another day," he added.
By Monday, the nationalist leaders had released a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to drive constitutional change.
They said no Westminster government has the right to block democratic decisions made by Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.
"Each of our nations has the right to determine its own future, through democratic means and in accordance with the wishes of its people," the three leaders wrote.

"For the first time ever, people across these islands have First Ministers in Scotland, in Wales and in the North of Ireland who are all committed to independence from the United Kingdom. For people watching across these islands – for people watching around the world – there could be no clearer sign that Westminster’s time is coming to an end," the statement continued.
MEET 'COUNT BINFACE,' THE TRASH CAN-CLAD COMEDIAN CHALLENGING NIGEL FARAGE

Andy Burnham delivers his inaugural speech as UK's new Prime Minister on July 20, 2026 in London, England. The Member of Parliament for Makerfield becomes the UK's 59th Prime Minister, succeeding Sir Keir Starmer, who resigned as leader of the Labour Party and Prime Minister in June. (Photo by Dan Kitwood/Getty Images) (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)
"We call for the British Government to prepare for, plan and facilitate constitutional change in each jurisdiction," the memorandum said.
According to GB News, Burnham was told Monday that he could not stop the breakup of the U.K.
Sinn Féin, the largest party in the Northern Ireland Assembly, issued the warning after signing the memorandum with the SNP and Plaid Cymru.
O’Neill said the three nations shared a "common cause" because "Westminster does not and will never serve our people well."
She added during a news conference that Burnham would not be able to "hold back the tide" of nationalism.

"We’re certainly living in times of enormous change, change that is unstoppable, change that, no matter what is said by any British prime minister, will not be able to hold back the tide of what’s happening in front of our eyes right now.
"Our common cause here is the understanding that Westminster does not and will never serve our people well," she added.
KING CHARLES FOLLOWS QUEEN ELIZABETH'S PLAYBOOK WITH A TWIST DURING TRUMP STATE VISIT: EXPERT

President Donald Trump speaks with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin during a meeting in the Oval Office of the White House, on St. Patrick's Day, Tuesday, March 17, 2026, in Washington. (Alex Brandon/AP Photo)
The memorandum commits the parties to cooperation on economic policy, renewable energy and rebuilding ties with the European Union, among other areas.
It also calls for greater self-determination and states that the nations should work together as equals.
A spokesperson for Burnham said: "The Prime Minister is committed to delivering change across all four nations of the United Kingdom and believes strongly in the Union.

"The United Kingdom is at its best when people come together around our shared values and problem-solving, rather than division, and the Prime Minister will continue to ease pressures on household finances and delivering greater economic security, rather than engaging in constitutional debates or further referendums."

title: Russia readies new 500-mile missile as weapon expert warns of 'terminal end game surprises'
summary: Russia plans to test a new 800-km ballistic missile by year's end, with an analyst warning its advanced maneuverability could strain Ukraine air defense.
story: Defense analyst warns Moscow’s new missile may come with maneuvering capabilities or "terminal end game surprises".

Moscow is preparing for a final test of a new ballistic missile capable of striking targets hundreds of miles away and potentially maneuvering in ways that could challenge Ukraine’s already strained air defenses, a defense analyst warned Monday.
The warning comes as Ukrainian military officials said that Russia could conduct the test in the coming months and potentially in live-fire strikes.

"According to our estimates, Russia plans to conduct final tests of a new type of ballistic missile with a range of up to 800 km by the end of this year," Vadym Skibitskyi, deputy head of the Defence Intelligence of Ukraine (DIU), said at a meeting of the Ukraine-NATO Interparliamentary Council, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda.

"If, for instance, this 800-kilometer missile has more advanced maneuverability, well then that's going to create greater problems for Ukraine in that they're going to need the more sophisticated interceptors to get them," Tom Karako, director of the Missile Defense Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told Fox News Digital.
RUSSIA DEPLOYS NORTH KOREAN MISSILE UNIT TO UKRAINE; MOSCOW-PYONGYANG AXIS DEEPENS: REPORT
A Sarmat missile, also known as "Satan 2," is being fired from an undisclosed location in Russia. (East2West)
"This means terminal maneuvers that weave a little bit so that the defender doesn't quite know where it's going or what trajectory it will have," Karako said.
"Another possibility is that they just figured out a way to make some kind of 800-kilometer missile more cheaply or in large numbers," the expert said of the Russians.
Karako said developments in precision-guided munitions, along with a broader shift away from unguided weaponry, could offer clues about the type of missile Russia will launch.
NEXT-GENERATION MISSILE DEFENSE AT MISSION SPEED
Ukrainian firefighters work to extinguish a fire at a market following a Russian missile strike in Kyiv.  (AFP)

"Everyone is going for increased maneuverability," Karako explained. "Just about every gravity bomb that we have has some kind of terminal guidance for precision," he said, specifically of the U.S. arsenal.
"In a similar way, a moment's not too far in the future where you don't really have that many purely ballistic missiles."
"You have things that may be ballistic for a good part of their path, but are also equipped with maneuvering reentry vehicles or some kind of terminal end game surprises," he warned.

Meanwhile, according to Ukraine's DIU, Russian forces may try to strike targets in western Ukraine during the missile tests as a live-fire demonstration, which Karako said is standard practice in wartime.
"This is a business-as-usual arrangement where you might do lots of developmental testing and then formally field and then have your operational testing," the expert said.
RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY
Smoke rises over Kyiv following a Russian missile and drone attack that struck multiple districts of the Ukrainian capital. July 8, 2026. (East2West news)

"There are all kinds of norms being broken, though, because it is, after all, wartime, and so it may well be the case that some of this stuff is tested — maybe not the first time — but some of the early tests are done, frankly, in the field in Ukraine," he added.
The missile would, however, fall into a category once prohibited under the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty, Karako warned.

Signed by President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev in 1987, the INF Treaty required the United States and the Soviet Union to eliminate ground-launched ballistic and cruise missiles with ranges between 500 and 5,500 kilometers (roughly 310 to 3,400 miles).
The United States withdrew from the treaty in 2019 amid alleged Russian violations.
"This range is one that was formerly prohibited by the INF Treaty that capped ballistic and cruise missiles at 500 kilometers in range," Karako said.
"To some extent, you see Russia filling that gap, which is understandable and reasonable. Of course, they were violating the INF Treaty, which was why the United States got out of it."
PENTAGON PLOTS NEW NUCLEAR OPTIONS FOR TRUMP AS AMERICA’S BIGGEST ADVERSARIES RAISE STAKES: REPORT
At the closing ceremony for the Geneva Summit, Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev and President Ronald Reagan sit near each other, on November 21, 1985. (Bettmann via Getty Images)

Missiles and artillery have been central to Russia's campaign against Ukraine since the start of the war in 2022. Ukrainska Pravda reported Aug. 10, citing Ukrainian military intelligence, that production of Russia's primary missile types had reached between 110% and 120% of monthly targets.
According to the Kyiv Independent, Russia fired at least 1,858 missiles of various types at Ukraine from the start of 2026 through Aug. 27.
"This is what's hitting Ukraine on a daily and weekly basis. And so it's in that broader context of that demand for standoffs of various kinds that you see new things pop up," Karako said.
RUSSIA THREATENS STRIKES ON UK MILITARY TARGETS, ‘CATASTROPHIC CONSEQUENCES’ OVER UKRAINE
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte (not seen) hold a joint press conference in Kyiv, Ukraine, on June 3, 2026. (Danylo Antoniuk/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy highlighted the growing strain on air defenses in an interview with Deutsche Welle at a Canadian military base in North Bay Sept. 12.

"I want to have 100-120 [interceptor missiles] for these difficult months, especially the cold months," Zelenskyy said. "We'll see how many months this winter lasts — that is, these cold months: one, two, three. We don't know. This is truly a major challenge."
"It is the case that Russia really is on a wartime footing, and they really have mobilized their defense industrial base to be cranking these (missiles) out like sausages," Karako said.
"There was a point in which everything was going to the front, everything was going to Ukraine."
"There have been other reports more recently that suggest that Russia may be keeping some in reserve," Karako added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"There are lots of worries. If you're in Poland, if you're in Romania, if you're in the Baltics, you're worried about the Russians."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Iran’s proxy money machine: How the Houthis built a multibillion-dollar network despite US sanctions
summary: The Houthis' advance toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait is fueled by a sprawling sanctions-evasion network spanning Iranian oil, crypto and Russia.
story: Adam Rousselle, founder of Between the Lines (BTL) Research, says Iran-backed Houthis have built a sprawling financial network spanning oil, ports, crypto, Russia and China — complicating U.S. efforts to choke off the money sustaining the group.

The Houthis’ rapid advance toward one of the world’s most important shipping chokepoints is putting fresh scrutiny on the sprawling financial network that has helped transform the Iran-backed group from a Yemeni insurgency into a heavily armed regional power capable of threatening global trade.

The group has seized new territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, including the strategic port city of Mocha, and expanded toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The waterway connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and carries a significant share of global maritime trade and energy shipments.

For the Trump administration, the Houthi advance is becoming as much a financial challenge as a military one. Washington is intensifying efforts to choke off the money sustaining Iran and its proxies, but the Houthis have built a sprawling sanctions-evasion network while controlling ports, trade routes and millions of Yemenis — raising a difficult question for Treasury: how do you cut off the cash fueling the group without cutting off food, fuel and other lifelines to civilians?
SAUDI ARABIA TELLS TRUMP NOW IS THE TIME FOR MILITARY ACTION AS IRAN-BACKED HOUTHIS ADVANCE

Yemen's Iran-backed armed Houthi group has warned they will move to shutter the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait through missile-drone attacks if Gulf nations join the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)
The Houthis operate a financial network that extends far beyond Yemen, according to Adam Rousselle, founder of Between the Lines Research.
"We’re dealing with a very well-capitalized group," Rousselle told Fox News Digital.

In a 2025 investigation for the Global Network on Extremism and Technology, Rousselle traced a financing system spanning Houthi-controlled ports, tariffs, Iranian oil, informal hawala networks, cryptocurrency exchanges and foreign facilitators across Russia, Turkey and Southeast Asia.

Control of ports has historically been central to Houthi revenue because Yemen depends heavily on imports. Rousselle’s GNET report said the Houthis have imposed steep fees at ports they control and tariffs on goods brought into their territory from rival Yemeni ports.
HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS
Satellite imagery shows Bab el Mandeb Strait, a key shipping waterway and the gateway to the Red Sea, in this handout picture dated July 12, 2026. (Nasa Worldview/Handout via Reuters)
The group’s latest territorial gains could strengthen that economic base even further.

Nadwa Al-Dawsari, a Yemen expert and associate fellow at the Middle East Institute, told lawmakers in Sept. 1 testimony before the House Foreign Affairs Committee that territory is central to the Houthis’ ability to withstand outside pressure.

"The most important source of that leverage is territory," Al-Dawsari testified. "The Houthis have been able to consolidate their power and build increasingly sophisticated military capabilities because they control significant territory, a large population, ports, infrastructure, and resources."
"That territorial base allows them to recruit, generate revenue, manufacture and store weapons, control smuggling routes, and regenerate capabilities degraded by airstrikes and sanctions," she added.
IRAN LOSES KEY ECONOMIC LIFELINE IN MIDDLE EAST THAT TRUMP'S SANCTIONS COULDN'T REACH AS DEADLOCK PERSISTS
Houthi supporters chant slogans during an anti-U.S. and anti-Israel rally in Sanaa, Yemen, March 17, 2025. (AP Photo/Osamah Abdulrahman)
Rousselle said the Houthis’ finances should not be understood simply as Tehran handing cash to an Iranian proxy.
"It’s a bit of a misunderstanding that the Iranians just give them money," he said, describing the Houthis instead as embedded in a broader Iranian commercial ecosystem.

"The Houthis aren't sanctions-proof; they're sanctions-adapted," Miad Maleki, senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital. "Most of their money is made inside Yemen — customs and taxes at Hodeidah and Ras Isa, and fuel above all."

Treasury has estimated that the Houthis generate more than $2 billion a year from oil sales, while Iran provides the group with a free monthly oil shipment through Iranian-owned or affiliated companies based in Dubai. Treasury has also documented Houthi revenue from taxes imposed on petroleum imports.
CHINA ORDERS FIRMS TO IGNORE US IRAN SANCTIONS, DARING US TO ENFORCE CRACKDOWN
Scott Bessent, Treasury secretary, departs following a tariff announcement in the Rose Garden of the White House on April 2, 2025. (Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Sanctions can't reach domestic extraction," Maleki said. "What they can reach is the plumbing between Sana'a and the outside world; the exchange houses, the Dubai and Muscat correspondents, the tankers and the wallets."

At the center of that system is Sa’id al-Jamal, whom the Treasury Department has identified as an Iran-backed Houthi financial official operating an international network that sells Iranian commodities and channels proceeds toward the group.

Treasury said in April 2025 that al-Jamal’s network had procured tens of millions of dollars in weapons, sensitive goods and commodities from Russia and identified eight digital-asset wallets used by the Houthis. Blockchain analytics cited in Rousselle’s GNET research identified nearly $900 million in outflows across those addresses.
Rousselle cautioned against treating that figure as a complete picture of Houthi wealth.
"The system is more important than the number itself," he said, describing the network as fluid and difficult to quantify.
Russia, he argued, has become a particularly significant part of the network. "The Russians are definitely more hands-on in their support," Rousselle said.
TRUMP TO CONFRONT XI AT HIGH-STAKES SUMMIT OVER CHINA BACKING FOR IRAN, RUSSIA
Houthi supporters demonstrate in solidarity with Iran, in Sanaa, Yemen, April 10, 2026. (Khaled Abdullah/Reuters)

Al-Dawsari’s congressional testimony similarly highlighted the Houthis’ expanding relationships beyond Iran, saying the group is "deepening ties with other U.S. adversaries, particularly Russia and China."

She cited reports that Russia provided targeting data used to help the Houthis attack Western ships in the Red Sea and that Russian petroleum products were transferred ship-to-ship into a Houthi-controlled tanker before reaching the Houthi-controlled port of Ras Isa.

The China connection is more complicated. Rousselle said Chinese-linked private commercial actors appear in parts of the network but distinguished that activity from proven direct Chinese government involvement.
"The Chinese are kind of… turning a blind eye," he said.

His GNET report described Iranian oil flowing to privately owned Chinese "teapot" refineries and examined transactions linked to Southeast Asian financial networks, while cautioning that the available evidence did not establish direct Chinese government control of Houthi financing.

Al-Dawsari pointed to a broader Chinese role in Houthi supply chains. Citing U.S. officials, she said a Chinese satellite company with ties to the Chinese military provided satellite imagery supporting Houthi attacks against U.S. warships and international shipping. She also cited interdiction data showing that 60% of the components and materials used in the Houthi Qasef-2K drone came from China, compared with roughly 15% from Iran.
That sprawling network is now testing Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s broader effort to isolate Tehran economically and disrupt the financial channels sustaining Iran and its proxies.
Rousselle said decentralized illicit-finance networks present a fundamental challenge.
"You’re dealing with a ‘you shut down one, another pops up’ kind of situation," he said.
Maleki argued that Washington should concentrate on the points where Houthi money intersects with the formal financial system.
IRAN TAPS FINANCIAL LIFELINE, RUSSIAN ARMS AS TRUMP ESCALATES 'CRUSHING' ECONOMIC WARFARE
Houthi supporters show solidarity with Palestinians in the Gaza Strip and to condemn U.S. strikes in Yemen, in Sanaa, Yemen May 30, 2025. (Reuters/Adel Al Khader)

"The soft spots are wherever Houthi money touches the formal system," he said. "Treasury has named the Yemeni banks and the Sana'a exchange houses that pay for missile components; it should now name the foreign correspondents still clearing for them. That is the one tool that changes behavior overnight."
Oman represents another potential pressure point. "Oman is the Houthis' land bridge and their mailing address," Maleki said.

But squeezing Houthi finances presents another dilemma: Yemen remains one of the world’s most fragile humanitarian environments, and the Houthis control ports and infrastructure through which civilians receive food, fuel and other basic goods.
"I would be lying if I had a concrete answer to it," Rousselle said when asked how Washington could disrupt Houthi revenue without worsening the humanitarian crisis.
IRAN-BACKED HOUTHI THREAT IN RED SEA COULD LEAD TO MAJOR US POLICY SHIFT, ANALYSTS SAY

Members of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces react during clashes with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis in a location given as near Al-Hazm, Yemen, in this screen grab obtained from a handout video released Sept. 9, 2026. (Media Centre Of The Yemeni Armed Forces/Handout via Reuters)
"The humanitarian argument is the Houthis' best shield, and it's backwards," Maleki said. "Food and medicine are licensed and should stay that way."
"Keep the goods flowing and take away the toll," he added, arguing that Washington should seek ways to prevent humanitarian trade from generating taxes and fees for Houthi authorities.
Rousselle warned that the challenge extends far beyond Yemen.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A map highlights the Yemeni port city of Hodeida on the Red Sea coast, where Israeli airstrikes targeted Houthi military infrastructure on Sept. 16, 2025. (Associated Press)
"This isn’t just about the Houthis," he said. "This is about any sanctioned actor worldwide capable of harnessing financial systems that are completely outside of regulatory control."
The Treasury Department did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Houthis enter US 'kill box' after seizing Red Sea 'cork,' former Pentagon official warns
summary: Houthi rebels seized Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, but a former Pentagon official warns they've entered a vulnerable U.S. Navy kill box.
story: Houthis seize Perim Island, exposing themselves to U.S. firepower, former Pentagon official says.

Iran-backed Houthi rebels captured Perim Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait Sept. 11, opening a new front at a vital global shipping chokepoint as a former Pentagon official warned Sunday the militants had entered a "kill box."

The island's capture came after a month-long offensive along Yemen’s western coast that killed more than 1,500 soldiers and forced Yemen’s government to acknowledge a "painful" defeat, according to The Associated Press.
"With Perim, they have gained what we could call the cork in the Red Sea bottle," Morgan Murphy, a former Pentagon press secretary and Navy Reserve captain, told Fox News Digital.

"But they've put themselves into a kill box. They're nowhere near the capability of the United States and if the president so chooses, he can wipe them off the face of that rock pretty easily," Murphy warned.
SAUDI ARABIA TELLS TRUMP NOW IS THE TIME FOR MILITARY ACTION AS IRAN-BACKED HOUTHIS ADVANCE
The Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on September 11 in a move to tighten their grip on a vital global shipping route. (Reuters)
Despite Perim sitting in the middle of the narrow maritime passage, Murphy detailed how the Houthis had effectively placed themselves in an area that is vulnerable to concentrated fire.
"Perim cuts that chokepoint right in half, and it's only 18 miles wide there," Murphy said.
He said the island has served as a pivotal maritime vantage point for hundreds of years, previously targeted for control by French forces and held by the British Empire for over a century.

Perim — a desolate volcanic island also known as Mayun — also sits roughly 20 miles off the Horn of Africa, placing it in proximity to Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, home to one of the largest U.S. military installations on the continent.
"We have incredible firepower in that region, and that's a little rock in the middle of that strait. It's a volcanic rock. It doesn't have any water. It's uninhabitable," Murphy warned.
"There's no vegetation to speak of. And the Houthis have just massed their troops on that rock. So what that is, what we would call that in the Navy, is a kill box."

Satellite imagery of the island shows a 1.85-kilometer (6,070-foot) runway alongside three military hangars, which regional intelligence reports attribute to past construction by the United Arab Emirates.
"There's a 6,000-foot airstrip on that island. I think that Emiratis built it," Murphy said.
‘GATE OF TEARS’ AT RISK: IRAN THREATENS MAJOR NEW GLOBAL CHOKEPOINT IF US MOVES ON HORMUZ

"It's nice to have an airstrip, and especially a long runway, but we don't know the condition of that runway. We don't know how they could possibly use that runway, and they certainly don't have the sophisticated air power that the United States and its allies have to project power from that runway."
He added that the U.S. military holds overwhelming force options if commanders elect to target the island.
"We could wipe that rock into glass, just blast it into a smooth glass surface, put skates back on our feet, and skate all over it," Murphy said.
"That's why the Houthis have kind of played coy with the president, and they know that even if they fortify that rock they're not going to be able to hold it in the face of the United States Navy."
The developments come amid diplomatic maneuvering between Washington, Riyadh and the Houthis in recent days.

Sources confirmed to Fox News Digital that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had called President Donald Trump twice Sept. 10 to urge him to authorize U.S. military strikes against Houthi positions.
Trump declined direct intervention, with U.S. officials noting the administration has no immediate plans for direct combat involvement but will continue offering intelligence assistance.
IRAN AND HOUTHI TERROR PROXY FACING RED SEA THREAT FROM PRO-US AFRICAN NATION

Satellite imagery shows Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping waterway and the gateway to the Red Sea, as Iran threatens using Yemen's Houthi allies to shut the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea, in this handout picture dated July 12, 2026. (Nasa Worldview/Handout via Reuters)
Speaking to reporters in Dublin on Sept. 12, Trump also indicated the Houthis had signaled a desire to avoid direct confrontation with American forces.
"The Houthis called us, and they don’t want to fight with us. They let us know, they don’t want to fight with us... they don’t want us to go after them," Trump said.
Murphy suggested, however, that Washington’s restraint should not be mistaken for inaction.
"I can't speak for the president. But this administration has not shown a lack of resolve to use force," Murphy said.
"I wouldn't doubt at all if the president took steps to pound some of these folks into the sand if they continue to really disrupt the global energy supply."

Yemeni government, regional and Iranian sources told Reuters the Houthi advance was sustained by Iranian weaponry and tactical direction from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC, with U.S. officials estimating hundreds of IRGC officers remain active in Yemen.
Murphy noted that Tehran's strategy appears designed to drive up global fuel prices by choking critical shipping lanes.
TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS

Protesters who support Yemen's Houthi group brandish weapons and shout slogans as they celebrate the ban imposed against the maritime shipping of Saudi Arabia on July 20, 2026, in Sana'a, Yemen. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)
Comparing the conflict to historical naval power struggles, Murphy emphasized the strategic mismatch.
"We're in a different era. They are nowhere near the sophistication of the world's major powers. The Houthis are using a 19th-century playbook. They are not using 21st-century warfare," he said.
"So, yes, they've caught a critical cork in the Red Sea bottle, but how they use it remains to be seen," Murphy concluded.

"This is an example of why great powers really have to have a strong Navy. This is why Great Britain had a strong navy. This is why the United States has a strong navy, because there's so many regional powers who want to try to bottle up shipping, whether it is in the Strait of Malacca, whether it is in the Strait of Hormuz, and here, in this case, in the Red Sea."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I think what we're going to see in the next several days and weeks is a coordinated effort by the Trump administration to make sure our allies are on board in helping us keep these critical waterways open, free, and clear for freedom of navigation," he said.
