title: Bystanders chase down man accused of striking woman with stolen car on San Diego boardwalk
summary: The 25-year-old woman was hospitalized in critical condition, officials said.
story: A man behind the wheel of a suspected stolen Tesla drove onto the Pacific Beach boardwalk in San Diego and struck a woman before he hopped out and was chased by bystanders Monday afternoon.

The 25-year-old woman was struck by the electric vehicle around 12:40 p.m. at the intersection of Thomas and Reed avenues and was transported to a hospital in critical condition, according to the San Diego Fire-Rescue Department.

Around 12:20 p.m., San Diego Police Department officers responded to a report of a stolen Tesla that its owner was tracking. About 10 minutes later, officers located the Tesla driving south on Mission Boulevard. Officers attempted to stop the driver, but he did not stop and the chase began, police said.
During the pursuit, the driver struck a San Diego Gas and Electric transformer and continued toward the Pacific Beach boardwalk, SDPD said.
“Due to the increasing risk to public safety, a field supervisor terminated the pursuit,” it said.
The stolen Tesla then traveled onto the boardwalk northbound from Pacific Beach Drive, driving fast near pedestrians.

“I just heard some sounds down there, commotion like something hit something, and obviously he hit a gal over here. And so that was the sound that I heard,” witness Miguel Valle said. “Then a moment later I see a navy blue Tesla flying by me at least 50 mph, trying to get away from the pursuit.”
Another woman was walking on the boardwalk but jumped out of the way right as the driver sped by, surveillance video shows. She was evaluated by emergency responders, SDFD said.
“A lot of people dove out of the way very quickly, and it really could have been so much worse,” SDFD spokesperson Candace Hadley said.
“This is a very busy boardwalk. Having someone drive through this area is incredibly frightening,” Hadley added.
Multiple people witnessed the car driving onto the boardwalk. One beachgoer from Santee described walking on the boardwalk when the car came rushing by him.
“I was in the middle of the path and I launched myself off my bike,” Alex Srour said.
The man driving the Tesla stopped the vehicle in front of the Baja Beach Cafe, and Srour ran after him, recording the chase on his Meta sunglasses, which have a built-in camera.
His video shows a couple of other people chasing after the man as he runs into a nearby parking lot and falls to the ground. Srour appears to pin him to the ground, and a verbal exchange ensues.
In the video, Srour yells at the man to get on the ground, and the man appears to plead with Srour.
Srour, along with other pedestrians, detained the man until officers arrived and took him into custody, SDPD said.
SDPD is conducting a felony hit-and-run investigation into the incident. The driver was suspected of being under the influence, police said.
Lifeguards initially responded to the incident, quickly followed by SDFD and SDPD. A woman who jumped out of the way is all right, the fire department said.
Police blocked off the area of Thomas Avenue and Mission Boulevard near Open Bar for several hours following the incident. By 4 p.m., the boardwalk had reopened.

title: Putin-linked Russian oligarch paid for Donald Trump Jr.’s lavish island wedding party
summary: The president’s eldest son and his wife, Bettina Trump, said Umar Kremlev “very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations” after their wedding.
story: Donald Trump Jr. and his wife, Bettina Trump, acknowledged Monday that a Russian oligarch with ties to President Vladimir Putin paid for their lavish Caribbean island post-wedding celebration in May.

ProPublica reported that Umar Kremlev paid hundreds of thousands of dollars in wedding-related expenses for the newlyweds and dozens of guests for festivities on a private island in the Bahamas that started a day after the ceremony. The festivities included a fireworks show, which ProPublica reported Kremlev also paid for.

“Our dear friend Umar very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding. It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend, and something for which we were and remain incredibly grateful,” according to a post on Bettina Trump’s Instagram page, which was signed “Don & Bettina.”

It’s unclear why a member of the Trump family — who has made hundreds of millions of dollars during the first year of his father’s second term, some of it from cryptocurrency ventures that have involved foreign investments — would accept a gift from someone so closely aligned with Putin.
President Donald Trump, who did not attend the wedding or the celebration, told NBC News in a statement that it was “not a big deal.”

“I have no idea who Umar is, never heard of him, and he didn’t pay for Don and Bettina’s wedding, which took place at a totally different location, and on a different day from the wedding. It was an ‘afterparty’ given in their honor. Not a big deal! I was not present at the party,” the statement said.

The top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, Robert Garcia of California, said on X that Kremlev, who has been sanctioned by the Ukrainian government, “spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on the President’s son. What did he get in return? We need answers.”

On her Instagram page, Bettina Trump said the island vacation, which included other members of the Trump family, had “been planned well in advance as a fun weekend with friends. It was never intended to be our wedding weekend. When our original wedding plans changed, we simply decided to get married before it and arrived at an already planned weekend as newlyweds.”
She also insisted there was nothing untoward about Kremlev’s involvement.

“It’s unfortunate that something so personal and happy can be recast as something political or sinister simply because of who someone is or where they come from. Friendship doesn’t require a political motive. Generosity doesn’t automatically come with an agenda. And sometimes a wedding gift is simply a wedding gift,” she wrote.

It’s not clear how long Kremlev, who is president of the International Boxing Association, and Trump Jr. have known each other. They both appeared at one of the organization’s events in Turkey last September.
“I am proud to call Umar not only a leader but a friend,” Trump Jr. said at the time.
Kremlev said that they were “joining forces” and that “together, we will protect the transparency of boxing and open the door for the next generation.” He did not elaborate on how they were uniting.
Representatives for Kremlev and Trump Jr. did not immediately respond to requests for comment for this article.

Kremlev became head of the IBA in 2020. The association’s website says Putin presented Kremlev with an Order of Friendship medal in late April for his “contribution to international sport and his commitment to the global boxing family.”
Shortly before the Trump wedding, Kremlev was part of the Russian delegation that went with Putin to Beijing for a discussion of the future of boxing in China, according to Chinese state media.
Trump Jr. has met with people with ties to Putin.

Then-special counsel Robert Mueller scrutinized him during his father’s first term over a meeting he had amid the 2016 presidential campaign with a person who he was told was the “crown prosecutor of Russia” and had dirt on Democratic nominee Hillary Clinton.

Trump Jr. responded to the offer in an email saying, “if it’s what you say I love it especially later in the summer.” The meeting with a Kremlin-linked lawyer and other Russians with ties to Putin took place at Trump Tower in June 2016 but did not yield any helpful information for the campaign, according to Mueller’s report.

While it is illegal for campaigns to accept help from foreign governments or from foreign nationals, Mueller declined to bring any charges in that part of the probe, because his investigators did not believe they could prove Trump Jr. acted “willfully” when he possibly violated campaign finance law.

Trump Jr.’s attorney, Alan Futerfas, said in 2019 in response to Mueller’s report that it confirmed that the meeting “was just what Don said it was, and nothing more, and that there was nothing improper about potentially listening to information.”

title: Supreme Court says Trump can’t enforce new mail-in ballot regulation
summary: The decision means a Postal Service measure that could lead to ballots not being sent to voters won’t be in effect for this November’s midterm elections.
story: WASHINGTON — Casting a decisive blow against President Donald Trump’s hopes of exercising federal control over the midterm elections, the Supreme Court on Monday prevented a U.S. Postal Service regulation concerning mail-in ballots from going into effect.

The court in a brief order rejected an emergency application the Trump administration filed seeking to block a lower court ruling that said the regulation was most likely unlawful. The court appeared to be divided 7-2, with two conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, dissenting.
The measure would have imposed requirements on states for sending out mail-in ballots to voters. Typically, the Postal Service has no such role.

Implementing those significant changes just weeks before the election would most likely have caused major problems, and advocates feared it would make it harder for millions of Americans to cast their ballots.

Time was already running out for the rule to be implemented, with North Carolina sending out ballots Sept. 4 and other states following suit. There were also questions about whether the Postal Service even had the technical means to put it into effect.

Challengers, including various states led by California and nonprofit advocacy groups headed by the League of Women Voters, said the rule would cause unnecessary disruption ahead of the election and prevent people from voting.

“Today’s decision is a victory for our democracy and a powerful affirmation of the rule of law,” California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement. “The stakes in this litigation could not have been higher.”
In a separate statement, Celina Stewart, CEO of the League of Women Voters, called the regulation “an extraordinary attempt to interfere with voting in all 50 states.”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment Monday night.
Trump frequently rails against the widespread use of mail-in ballots as part of his broader complaints, offered without evidence, that the election system is rife with fraud.

Under the new rule, states would have to submit lists of eligible voters to the Postal Service, which would then verify that ballots were being sent to people on that list before it delivered them. States would also have to comply with directions about envelope design.

Trump’s initial order envisioned the federal government creating and sending the Postal Service lists of citizens and forcing it to send ballots to those people, but the final Postal Service proposal did not include that provision.

In a dissenting opinion, Alito said the federal government had the better of the argument. Concerns raised by states about the difficulties of implementing the rule gave him pause, he added, “but it is not enough to convince me.”
Alito also complained that courts, including the Supreme Court itself, were partly to blame for the case being decided so close to the election, saying they had taken too long to decide it.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh, another member of the court’s conservative majority, wrote a brief concurring opinion saying there is a “fair prospect” the Postal Service has the authority to issue the rule but added it had to be blocked because it was issued so close to the election.
The Postal Service issued the regulation at the direction of the White House, with Trump issuing an executive order about the issue in March.
Massachusetts-based U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani blocked the regulation, saying the Postal Service had no authority to issue it.

She warned of the risk of “significant disenfranchisement” if the regulation were in effect and noted that the Trump administration had failed to offer any evidence that it was required to combat election fraud.

Various states have said they would not be able to comply with the regulation even if it were in effect, although some have indicated they could. A whistleblower complaint last week said the Postal Service system for checking ballots was flawed and that it could cause significant disruptions if it were implemented.

Talwani said that while litigation continues, states can voluntarily comply with the Postal Service regulation but have no obligation to do so. She also said the Postal Service cannot refuse to send ballots.

The federal government has downplayed the impact of the regulation, saying in court papers that it is a “modest design and information requirements for ballot-mail envelopes.” When states send out ballots, the Postal Service would check to see that the envelopes were in compliance, and if they were not, they would be returned to election officials, Trump administration lawyers said.

Trump issued his executive order after he failed to persuade the Republican-controlled Congress to pass his SAVE America Act legislation, which would impose new voting restrictions nationwide, including proof of citizenship to register to vote and voter ID.
Talwani had earlier blocked key provisions of the executive order itself, but in an Aug. 24 ruling, the Supreme Court ruled she had acted prematurely.

title: Gavin Newsom says he won’t run for president in 2028 if Kamala Harris does
summary: The California governor said there was too much “crossover” between his base and Harris’, and that it would be an electoral “gift” for everybody else if they both ran.
story: California Gov. Gavin Newsom made a surprise announcement that he won’t launch a 2028 White House bid if former Vice President Kamala Harris decides to run again.
“I wouldn’t run if she ran,” Newsom told CNN in an interview that aired Monday evening.
Newsom said running against Harris, a fellow California Democrat who was the state’s attorney general before she became a senator, would be an electoral “gift” for everybody else.

“They’d enjoy the hell out of it. Mutual assured destruction. It services no greater good. Why would I do this if I wasn’t trying to serve some greater good? There would be no upside whatsoever,” said Newsom, who has been considering a White House run.
Newsom, who has not run for president before, acknowledged that an “approach to the campaign” would be to say Harris, who ran in 2020 and 2024, had had a shot and has previously run for president.
“That would be the case you’d make. Pretty good one, actually. You know, that’s objectively true,” Newsom said, adding that the Venn diagram between them had too much crossover.
“I know her base of supporters; I know her friends,” Newsom said. “I wouldn’t do that to people.”
Harris’ office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Newsom’s remarks.
Newsom’s office did not immediately respond to a request for additional comment on his CNN remarks.
Harris has not said whether she will launch a bid for 2028. She said in July that she has “not made a decision” and that she is focused on the midterm elections.
Harris said this year that she was weighing making a third presidential run, telling the Rev. Al Sharpton at an April event that she was “thinking about it.”

Newsom, whose term as governor is up in a few months, had previously said he would decide whether to run after the midterms, telling CBS News last year that he would seriously consider the notion after the 2026 elections. He recently traveled to South Carolina — the first state to hold a Democratic primary in 2028 — and confirmed he was considering a presidential run.

title: Trump calls Nvidia CEO to talk AI — and gets put on speakerphone during industry summit
summary: “Data centers are great, and they make people wealthy,” the president told CEO Jensen Huang, whose company makes AI chips and hardware.
story: President Donald Trump on Monday called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during an industry summit and gave another full-throated defense of artificial intelligence after Huang put the call on speakerphone.
Trump characterized concerns about AI safety as a “hoax,” while telling Huang in the middle of the All-In Summit that the U.S. had to beat China in AI innovation and development.

“The robots will not be taking over. The AI will not be taking over the rest of the world. The whole thing is a hoax,” Trump said, suggesting that critics are “just playing right into the hands of a lot of people that don’t want to see it happen. That could be political people, that could also be China.”
Trump also lauded politically unpopular data centers, calling them “great” and saying they make people and states “wealthy.”
“It’s the oil of the next 20, 25 years, it’s bigger than the internet and AI, you know, much more so,” he said, while adding that people “have to be a little careful” and do things “prudently.”

A video of Trump’s call, posted on X, was reposted by the Trump War Room account, which is associated with a Trump-aligned PAC. The call is also included in a podcast that Huang was recording at the time.
Nvidia said it had no comment on Huang’s exchange with Trump or whether they will be meeting soon to discuss these issues.
Add to Google
Add to Google
Trump’s comments to Nvidia, one of the world’s biggest manufacturers of AI chips and hardware, come as AI leaders have called for slowing down development of the technology.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote in an essay over the weekend that AI development needed safeguards, which was quickly endorsed by Tesla CEO Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, among others. It came after researchers at leading AI companies stepped down from their jobs last week and spoke out over safety concerns, some describing them as an existential threat to humanity.
Former President Barack Obama urged Democrats last week to prioritize the development of an AI agenda.
Trump, however, has firmly stood by his support for AI development. In a flurry of social media posts Monday, Trump described AI concerns as a “SICK conspiracy” and a “hoax.”
During the Nvidia phone call, Trump said he assumed Huang was on the same page as him regarding AI development; Huang said they were.
“We’re going to make sure that everybody wins in the AI race in America. Every industry, every company, every state, every people,” he told Trump during their call.

The Nvidia CEO, who helped persuade Trump last year to not send National Guard troops to San Francisco, sits on Trump’s council of science and technology advisers. He has lobbied lawmakers to allow sales of Nvidia around the world, which lawmakers have said could advantage China and undercut U.S. leadership in technology.

His conversation with Trump came as House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., who had been urged by House Democrats to end recess early so the lower chamber could take legislative action regarding AI safety, said this week that industry leaders should be the ones taking the lead on safety.

Johnson said Monday that Trump would call a meeting with AI leaders. A source familiar with the matter told NBC News that a meeting between Trump and the leaders was “in the works,” but no clear timing had been nailed down.

CORRECTION (Sept. 14, 2026, 10:39 p.m. ET): A previous version of this article and its headline misstated the event where Trump spoke by phone to Nvidia’s CEO. It was during the All-In Summit, not during an all-hands meeting at Nvidia.

title: Trump loyalist subpoenaed John Brennan before resignation last week
summary: The former CIA director’s team is trying to persuade a federal judge in D.C. to force the Justice Department to preserve records it may use to make vindictive prosecution accusations.
story: A Trump loyalist heading a “grand conspiracy” investigation into some of President Donald Trump’s grievances signed a subpoena seeking testimony from former CIA Director John Brennan just before he resigned from the Justice Department last week, his lawyer told a court Monday.

On Wednesday, Joe diGenova signed the document aimed at Brennan for testimony before a federal grand jury in Fort Pierce, Florida, Brennan attorney Ken Wainstein wrote in a declaration. After Wainstein reached out to diGenova after he accepted the subpoena Thursday, diGenova wrote that he would “arrange counsel” to speak with them. Brennan’s testimony was preliminarily set for Oct. 15.

DiGenova resigned later Thursday. On Friday, Wainstein said, 2020 election denier Kurt Olsen — now part of the prosecutorial team in the Southern District of Florida — told Brennan’s team that there were multiple “viable” grand jury investigations into his client, “including a ‘far-reaching’ investigation in Fort Pierce that includes ‘issues at Mar-a-Lago and beyond’ into whether President Donald Trump had his civil rights violated.” Another investigation is running out of Washington, D.C., looking into Brennan’s statements before Congress, Olsen confirmed.

“Mr. Olsen explained that Director Brennan was a ‘target’ of the narrower investigation, and the investigation for which he was now being subpoenaed was the ‘more wide-ranging conspiracy,’ as to which our client was a ‘subject.’ However, he explained that the narrower investigation was ‘still viable,’ and that the issues in the narrower investigation might also be part of the larger investigation, such as being overt acts,” Wainstein wrote.

Wainstein and co-counsel Daniel Gelber appeared in court Monday before U.S. District Judge Jia M. Cobb in Washington to urge Cobb to order the Justice Department to preserve communications about the Brennan case.

Brennan’s team, citing reports of the Trump administration’s widespread use of Signal to conduct official government business, is seeking an injunction to force the government to preserve communications for a potential future argument that the case is a vindictive prosecution driven by Trump.

“Director Brennan seeks nothing more than to ensure that the government does what it is already obliged to do — preserve all records and communications relevant to the government’s preordained decision to investigate and prosecute him,” his team wrote in a filing last month.
“The government is not going to disclose what it’s destroying,” Wainstein said in court Monday. “There’s a lot of really underhanded stuff going on in this investigation.”

Wainstein also said that the Justice Department had been playing “games” with the case and that it was engaging in a “pretty unprecedented example of judge shopping” by running the federal grand jury probe from the courthouse in Fort Pierce in the Southern District of Florida, where Trump-friendly U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon is the sole judge.
Public officials are operating lawfully and honestly in discharging their official duties, and they’re not entitled to regular rules, Wainstein argued.
“If anything, it’s a presumption of irregularity,” he said.

Wainstein argued that diGenova was the “strongest champion” of a case against Brennan — noting that diGenova called Brennan a “traitor” a few years ago — and that his departure sent “a very clear message” about the case. DiGenova didn’t answer a phone call Monday.

Jeremy Newman, an attorney with the Justice Department, argued that the Justice Department conceded that it had a legal obligation to maintain some communications under the Federal Records Act but that Brennan was making an argument that his constitutional rights were violated and that he lacked standing to bring the suit given that he hadn’t been charged. If he were charged, Newman said, he could take those issues up with a judge and seek remedies.

Brennan’s team argued that will be too late, because any Signal messages exchanged about the case will have long disappeared. Wainstein suggested Justice Department leaders were using disappearing messages because they don’t want “history to know about what they were saying to one another” about what he called a politically driven investigation.
NBC News reported in May that the FBI was interviewing current and former CIA officers as part of the investigation.

DiGenova told NBC News on Friday that a specific event sparked his departure but wouldn’t go into details about the matter. “Everybody was in their lane, and then some lanes got crossed, and then I decided to leave,” he said.

After diGenova’s departure, the investigation is being run by the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida, Jason Reding Quiñones, with support from Main Justice, according to a person familiar with the matter.

title: October Prime Day dates were just announced — here’s everything you need to know
summary: Prime Big Deal Days is Amazon’s second Prime Day-level sale of 2026 for loyalty members. These are the dates and details to know, plus what to expect.
story: Amazon just confirmed that Prime Big Deal Days (unofficially dubbed October Prime Day 2026) is happening from October 6 to 7. The Prime member-exclusive sale gives shoppers 48 hours to stock up on household essentials and fall and winter staples, as well as get a head start on holiday shopping before popular items sell out. In fact, early October Prime Day deals are already live.

To help you plan for Prime Big Deal Days, I answered the most important questions below — I’ve been covering Amazon’s mega sales for seven years, so I know all the ins and outs, and I’ve been talking to experts for weeks about their expectations. Read on for everything you need to know and bookmark this article: I’ll share frequent updates as I learn more about October Prime Day.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
When is October Prime Day?
October Prime Day 2026 is from October 6 to 7. Amazon previously hosted Prime Big Deal Days around these dates, so this timing is typical for the retailer.
What time does October Prime Day start?
October Prime Day starts at 12 a.m. PT on October 6 — that’s 3 a.m. ET, 2 a.m. CT and 1 a.m. MT.
When does October Prime Day end?
October Prime Day ends on October 7 at 11:59 p.m. PT — that’s October 8 at 2:59 a.m. ET, 1:59 a.m. CT and 12:59 a.m. MT.
How long is October Prime Day?
October Prime Day is 48 hours long. It’s shorter than Prime Day, which has been four days long since 2025 and typically happens in July (but took place in June in 2026).
Do you need to be a Prime member to shop October Prime Day deals?

Yes, only Prime members can take advantage of the deals during Prime Big Deal Days. You can sign up for a free 30-day trial Prime membership on Amazon’s website or app (learn about the three different types here). Amazon automatically charges you for your Prime membership once the free trial ends.
Can you shop early October Prime Day deals?

Yes, Prime members can shop early October Prime Day deals as the event approaches — some are even live right now, which I’m tracking here. The best way to stay updated about early Prime Day deals is to download the Amazon app, which can notify you about sales in real-time.
What are the best deals on October Prime Day?

Products across all shopping categories are on sale during Prime Big Deal Days, but you won’t know exactly what’s available until the event starts. In my experience covering October Prime Day, the best deals are very similar to those you see during Prime Day in the summer: They center around Amazon-owned technology like Echo, Fire, Blink and Ring devices, small home and kitchen appliances, beauty products, household basics and groceries.

Additionally, because Prime Big Deal Days is in the fall, it unofficially kicks off the holiday shopping season, so brands discount popular gifts like gift cards and toys, as well as Advent calendars and themed decor. You’ll also be able to shop Amazon’s Lightning Deals during the event: They’re flash sales that give shoppers a short window to purchase limited quantities of specific products.

I recommend browsing through Amazon’s early October Prime Day deals to get a sense of what’s going to be discounted, and looking at bestsellers from previous years. In 2025, for example, NBC Selected readers saved a lot of money on the household essentials below, plus other favorites.

What is Prime Big Deal Days?

Prime Big Deal Days is Amazon’s second Prime Day-level sale of the year. The first one was in October 2022, and ever since, the retailer has hosted it around the same time each year. That’s why many people refer to Prime Big Deal Days as October Prime Day.

Like Prime Day, Prime Big Deal Days is exclusive to Prime members and offers some of Amazon’s lowest prices of the year across all product categories. But since the sale is in October rather than June or July, there’s an emphasis on early holiday shopping, so brands intentionally discount popular gifts like toys, gift cards, beauty sets and personal tech, as well as themed decor.
What is Amazon Prime?

Amazon Prime is the retailer’s loyalty membership program. You can get a free 30-day free trial, and after that, a standard membership costs $139 a year or $14.99 a month. Amazon also offers two types of discounted accounts: Prime for Young Adults, which is $7.49 a month for those 18 to 24 years old, and Prime Access, which is $3.50 for the first three months, and then $6.99 a month for those who qualify for certain government assistance programs.

Benefits of a Prime membership include exclusive savings during Prime Day and Prime Big Deal Days, as well as free two-day, one-day and same-day delivery. Prime members also get a handful of streaming and entertainment perks, plus they can order groceries online through Whole Foods or Amazon Fresh and sign up for a free Grubhub+ membership.
Is Prime Day twice a year?

Amazon has hosted two Prime Day-level events every year since 2022: Amazon Prime Day during the summer (typically July, but it was in June this year) and Prime Big Deal Days during the fall (typically in October, often referred to by shoppers as fall or October Prime Day). The retailer is following this schedule in 2026.
Why trust NBC Selected?

I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered Amazon since 2020. In addition to numerous sales stories, I wrote NBC Selected’s history of Amazon Prime Day and Prime membership guide, both of which I frequently update. I also regularly appear in related NBC News NOW and TODAY segments. For this article, I researched Prime Big Deal Days 2026 and reviewed information from Amazon press releases.

title: How to Watch the ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Premiere
summary: “Dancing with the Stars” returns to the ballroom with a special two-night Season 35 premiere on Tuesday, Sept. 15 and Wednesday, Sept. 16.
story: “Dancing with the Stars” returns to the ballroom with a special two-night Season 35 premiere on Tuesday, Sept. 15 and Wednesday, Sept. 16.

Sixteen new celebrities, including Jenna Dewan, Ciara Miller, Julia Stiles, Tatyana Ali and Taylor Hanson, will join their professional dance partners to compete for the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.
Judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough return to critique the teams alongside co-hosts Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough

The two-hour “Premiere: Night One” episode will feature only the competition’s male celebrities dancing to a No. 1 song from the year they were born. One celebrity will be eliminated at the end of the night.

On the two-hour “Premiere: Night Two” episode, the female celebrities will make their competition debut, performing to a No. 1 song from the year they were born, with one female star eliminated at the end of the night.
Here’s how to tune in every night, and what style and song each couple is dancing for Week 1.

The two-hour Season 35 “Premiere: Night One” episode of “Dancing With the Stars” begins on Tuesday, Sept. 15 at 8 p.m. ET/PT and 7 p.m. CT.
“Premiere: Night Two” airs Sept. 16 at 8 p.m. ET/PT and 7 p.m. CT.
Where to Watch the ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Premiere
Both nights of the Season 35 premiere will be broadcast live on ABC and Disney+ in local time zones. The episodes will also be available to stream the next day on Hulu.

title: Yes, Witney Carson Is Pregnant. And Yes, She Will Still Be Competing on ‘DWTS’: ‘It’s a Big Blessing to Do Both’
summary: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35.
story: On Aug. 17, “Dancing With the Stars” announced that pro dancer Witney Carson would be paired with Guillermo Rodriguez for Season 35. That same day, she revealed she was pregnant with her third child.

The announcement had many people wondering how she would be able to compete since the new season didn’t start for another month. But as Carson tells TODAY.com, she and husband Carson McAllister were set on expanding their family, and she didn’t think she needed to put her career on hold.

“We decided we wanted to grow our family. It’s time,” Carson, mom to sons Kevin, 5, and Jet, 3, says. “We know that we want a lot of kids and we thought it was a perfect year to start doing that. Then this opportunity came up again to do the show, and it just felt like, ‘You know what? I kind of want to prove to myself that I can do both!’ And I love both.”

Dancing since she was a child, Carson first gained fame after competing on Season 9 of “So You Think You Can Dance” in 2012.  The following year, she joined the “DWTS” troupe, before being promoted to a pro for Season 18 in 2014.

“I love to dance, and I love to compete, and I want to grow my family, as well,” the 32-year-old says. “I don’t feel like people necessarily have to lose parts of themselves to keep growing their family. That’s kind of my mantra. I’m gonna stay true to what I love and continue on my career and continue to grow my family. It’s a big blessing to be able to do both.”
For now, Carson is “feeling good,” listening to her body and making sure her baby’s healthy.

“As much as I want to dance and want to do all of it, I really have to be careful to make sure that I don’t overdo it,” she notes. “It’s perfectly safe to do all the things and I’m really not taking this any differently than I would any other season as far as mentally and physically.”

Taking it week by week, among her priorities is making sure she and her growing family are properly fueled. With a jam-packed schedule full of rehearsals and taking care of her boys with another on the way, Carson says she’s grateful for her Campbell’s partnership and the ability to make easy meals for her family.
“I remember my mom always making a hot meal with Campbell’s and so it’s very nostalgic for me,” she says. “It goes back to my childhood.”

Season 35 of “DWTS” kicks off on Sept. 15, which coincides with Campbell’s Two-Step Tuesdays launch celebrating its new sauces. Carson notes that after making a meal with the lemon garlic option, “Everyone gobbled it up ... I love to make dinner. I love doing that for my family. But I don’t have a lot of time, so being able to do something really simple like this two-step dinner is just an absolute dream.”
What is taking more than just two steps is preparing for her and Rodriguez’s competition debut. During the first episode, the duo will perform a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight.

“I’m really just having fun and Guillermo’s obviously very funny, he’s very heartwarming, he’s adorable,” she says of the “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” star. “He’s already so loved, and honestly, I’m really taking this season no differently than I would any other season. And I think people are a little surprised that you can continue to dance the way that I have.”

Last season, Carson took home her second Mirrorball trophy after coming in first place with Robert Irwin. While many might underestimate her and the comedian’s chances, she could go far depending on votes. (Let’s not forget how Andy Richter was dubbed “the People’s Princess” and made it to the quarterfinals.)

“There’s a TikTok floating around that’s ... not of me, but it’s of a pregnant woman and she’s got a big belly, and she’s break dancing on it,” Carson says. “And the meme is like, ‘Witney, when she makes it to the finale,’ and I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, literally!’”
With the possibility of her baby being crowned the youngest “DWTS” champ, Carson is ready for this new adventure.
“Listen, I’m prepared for it, kind of,” she says with a laugh. “I’ve never danced this far pregnant ... But listen, I will make it happen. I mean, I’m not injured. I’m just pregnant.”

summary: Read the first page of Emily St. John Mandel’s new novel “Exit Party.” The author breaks down the book’s setting and themes.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Emily St. John Mandel has always been interested in the aftermath of catastrophe.
The acclaimed author of “Station Eleven” doesn’t waste any time getting to that cataclysm on the opening page of her new novel, “Exit Party,” which hits stores on Sept. 15.
“In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace."
Mandel tells TODAY.com she wanted the novel’s very first line to have a “shock effect.”

“I just wanted to avoid confusion and plunge the reader immediately into this world I was creating,” Mandel tells TODAY.com. “It’s a very fast opening. We have the U.S. coming undone in literally the first sentence.”

It’s a theme Mandel has long explored in her work. In her 2014 bestseller “Station Eleven,” a group of survivors try to preserve art and human connection after the world is devastated by a deadly pandemic.
In “Exit Party,” a pair of connected storylines depict an “A side” of America splintered by civil war and a “B side” of a U.S. completely under totalitarian rule.

“I first started writing in the spring of 2022, and it seemed clear to me that I was extrapolating from our current world on the A side, where division turns into conflict,” Mandel says. “But by the time I finished the book about a year ago, I felt like I was struggling to stay ahead of the news cycle on the B side, the authoritarian state. The idea of America where secret police pick people off the street and disappear them felt fictional in 2022.”

“Exit Party” imagines how humans will try to retain connection and resilience in extreme circumstances, whether by throwing parties, putting on plays or performing a concert in a time of war or repression. Mandel says she was inspired by a 2016 story during the civil war in Syria in which residents in the war-torn town of Daraya assembled a secret underground library.
“You just want the characters to find these moments of brightness and ways to feel like you’re doing more than just surviving,” Mandel says.

The novel involves the ongoing journey of Aria, a character from her 2009 novel “The Singer’s Gun,” who has been released after 18 years in prison to an America divided by warring factions in the year 2031. She wanders a fractured Los Angeles, where the fighting has subsided for now.

“I think it’s important to me to try to kind of lean into these times when even though everything is wrong, there are moments that are good,” Mandel says. “This feeling of desperate joy at the end of the world.”
A primary theme of the novel is impermanence. A catastrophe has happened, but the characters work to find their way through to the other side of it.

“This idea that nothing lasts forever, and something always comes next after terrible moments we live through,” Mandel says. “It’s a book about resilience. Can you be resilient in these objectively awful times, because nothing lasts forever. Can you find hope in a state of impermanence?”

For those who enjoyed the Emmy-nominated “Station Eleven” television series in 2021-2022 on HBO Max, “Exit Party” is also being made for television. The feature project was bought by Laika Studios and will be produced by Amy Hodge of Fruit Tree, a film and television production company co-founded by Oscar winner Emma Stone and her husband, Dave McCary.
This time, Mandel, who did not work on the TV adaptation of “Station Eleven,” is adapting “Exit Party” for the screen.

“It’s been a challenge and fun,” she says. “I’ve always enjoyed revision, and for me, adaptation almost feels like a continuation of that. You realize pretty early on that you have to be willing to blow up the book to make it work onscreen.”
Read the First Page of Emily St. John Mandel’s ‘Exit Party’

In the first spring after the collapse of the United States, the blossoming of the jacaranda trees felt to Ari like grace. The trees bloomed in the same week that international peacekeeping troops withdrew from Los Angeles, and the convergence of flowers with the absence of foreign soldiers brought a delirious kind of hope. Everyone in the spring of 2031 knew the city was one terrorist attack away from disaster, but that peril made the season more vivid, not less.

It was Ari’s first spring outside of prison in nearly two decades, and she spent hours at a time walking the streets. Prison is a wasteland of sensory deprivation, and now the city was overwhelming. She kept expecting that the details of the world would cease to be extraordinary, but that kept not happening. No one around her seemed to notice the jacarandas, because in Los Angeles there are flowers every month of the year, but she walked streets where the trees were lit up by purple-blue blossoms and thought, My god. This place. She was forty-eight years old but felt younger, because so much of the world was new.

The United States had come undone following a coup d’état. Several states had seceded within a week of the coup, either alone or in alliances with neighbors, and war had broken out within the month. Now the fighting had subsided, for the most part, and Ari had been released into an uneasy aftermath.

title: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner Receive Moving Tributes During 2026 Emmys ‘In Memoriam’
summary: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.
story: Catherine O’Hara and Rob Reiner received tributes at the 2026 Emmy Awards’ “In Memoriam” segment led by performers who were close to each of them.

O’Hara’s former co-stars — Macaulay Culkin of “Home Alone” and Annie Murphy and Dan Levy of “Schitt’s Creek — celebrated the late actor in an emotional moment that began the segment. To start, Culkin, who as a child actor played O’Hara’s character’s son in the movie franchise, described the special connection the two shared.
Follow live coverage of the 2026 Emmys

“She was encouraging. She was warm. She was funny, but the word that I think of is ‘mama.’ You know, she wasn’t just a wife and mother to Beau and Matthew. She was my mom. She was our mom, and by extension, she’s all of her mom,” Culkin said.
“She may have forgotten me, twice,” Culkin said, poking fun at the movies’ plots, “but we will always remember her.”
Murphy, who with Levy played the adult kids of O’Hara’s character in “Schitt’s Creek,” said O’Hara’s laugh “challenged anyone who heard it to join in and be as delighted as she was.”
Levy said the most important lesson he learned from O’Hara was to “say yes” to new challenges and adventures, including the joyful creation of her quirky bewigged character Moira Rose.

“Say yes to her naming that wig,” Levy said. “Say yes to giving her space to experiment and create. It will amaze you on a daily basis, and it will change your life. Say yes to her dinner invites and her stories and her wisdom and her generosity.”

Later during the “In Memoriam” segment, Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Noah Kahan performed Simon & Garfunkel’s hit 1970 ballad “Bridge Over Troubled Water” as viewers saw images of other beloved stars who died over the past year, including Dolly Parton, James Van Der Beek, Hayden Panettiere, Eric Dane and more.
On the red carpet before the ceremony, Kahan explained to TODAY’s Sheinelle Jones why he chose to sing “Bridge Over Troubled Water” for Parton and others.
“It’s always represented so much hope and peace and kindness, which I think Dolly personified throughout her life and career,” said Kahan.

“We lost so many legends this year. I am really excited to get the chance to help memorialize them and to pay the respect to those who have contribute to this amazing industry and to art and culture,” added the singer.
The “In Memoriam” segment ended with a tearful Jamie Lee Curtis honoring late creator and director James Burrow and Hollywood director Rob Reiner, who she called a “cherished legend.”
Reiner got his start in television as an actor on “All in the Family” in the 1970s. Curtis described Reiner as “generous and kind and funny as hell and a friend to all.”
Last week, Reiner won a posthumous Emmy for a guest role on “The Bear,” Curtis revealed, breaking a record his father, comedy giant Carl Reiner, had held for longest time in between Emmy wins.
Reiner’s last Emmy award for acting came 48 years ago for “All in the Family.”

title: Reba McEntire Honors Dolly Parton at 2026 Emmys With Touching Cover Performance
summary: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.
story: Sally Field and Reba McEntire paid a special tribute to their late longtime friend Dolly Parton at the 2026 Emmys.

“If there are truly angels on earth then we just lost one: Dolly Parton,” said Field, who co-starred alongside Parton, Julia Roberts, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis and Daryl Hannah in the 1989 comedy “Steel Magnolias.”
“I adored her from day one and how could you not?” said Field. She remembered Parton, who died Aug. 25 at age 80 after a brief cancer battle, as “blisteringly funny.”
“She was genuine and humble and supportive,” Field said before acknowledging Parton’s humanitarianism had “made a profound difference” in the lives of many around the country.
“God bless you, Dolly Parton. I am not the only one on earth who will love you forever and forever,” Field said before footage of Parton appeared onscreen.
McEntire then took the stage to perform Parton’s ballad “Appalachian Memories.”
After Parton’s family announced her death, McEntire was among the first celebrities to pay tribute in an emotional Instagram post.
“There will never ever be another you,” McEntire wrote alongside a gallery of images of the longtime friends. “We will remember and cherish every memory and every note you ever played and sang.”
“She’s gonna have a blast in heaven singing all her favorite songs with all her family and friends who have gone on before her,” she added.
McEntire revealed during a “MasterClass” session on country music that she first met the Queen of Country in September 1977 backstage at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.
McEntire, who was scheduled to make her debut at the famed venue that night, learned the performance would be cut short because Parton, already a major star, had shown up unannounced.

“So I walked in, and they said, ‘Reba, I’m terribly sorry, but the two songs that we said you could sing, you’re only going to get to sing one. I said, ‘Why?’ And they said, ‘Well, Dolly Parton just pulled in the parking lot, and she’s going to take one of your songs.”
Rather than feel slighted, McEntire was thrilled.
“I said, ‘OK, can I meet her?!’” she recalled, laughing. “I didn’t care or anything. I just wanted to see Dolly Parton.”
McEntire also recalled seeing Parton for the first time backstage.
“She came walking in and I kind of backed up against the wall, and she had on the most beautiful black chiffon pantsuit with rhinestone butterflies on them and her beautiful hair,” McEntire said.
“I thought, ‘My gosh, that’s probably what an angel looks just like right there.”

title: Taylor Swift Attends Chiefs Season Opener Alongside Tom Cruise
summary: Find out if Taylor Swift attended the Chiefs vs Broncos game at Arrowhead Stadium on Sept. 14, 2026.
story: After a summer filled with love and celebration, Travis Kelce is switching his focus to the football field as his Kansas City Chiefs are set to take on the Denver Broncos in their opener to the 2026 NFL season.

The star tight end and Taylor Swift tied the knot in July at Madison Square Garden, surrounded by their family and A-list friends. Since then, Travis Kelce has been sharing a few details about the nuptials, in between discussing his hopes for the Chiefs’ season with brother Jason Kelce on their “New Heights” podcast. Now that football is officially back, the newlywed, who is entering his 14th season, is looking toward his team’s championship aspirations.
Throughout the season, he’ll likely have his bride cheering him on from the stands, where she has been frequently spotted at both home and away games since the two started dating in 2023.

The pop icon made an appearance at the season opener on Sept. 14, marking her return to Arrowhead Stadium since saying “I do”. She was photographed celebrating multiple touchdowns with Tom Cruise by her side.
Here’s what we know about the game and Swift’s attendance.
When Do the Chiefs and Broncos Play?
The Kansas City Chiefs will kick off their 2026 NFL season against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium on Monday, Sept. 14. It will be the last game of Week 1.
What Time Do the Chiefs and Broncos Play?
The game, which will see the teams go head to head for the first time since the Broncos defeated the Chiefs on Christmas Day last year, will begin at 5:15 p.m. PT/8:15 p.m. ET.
How to Watch and Stream the Chiefs-Broncos Game?
The game will air live simultaneously on ABC and ESPN. Fans who want to stream the game can watch via Disney+.
Was Taylor Swift at the Chiefs-Broncos Game?
Yes, Swift was spotted at the Sept. 14 game between the Chiefs and Broncos. She watched the matchup with Tom Cruise. The two hugged and high-fived when the Chiefs scored.

title: Taylor Swift Appears Alongside Mariska Hargitay in Emmys ‘SVU’ Sketch
summary: Mariska Hargitay seemingly used her pull as host of the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards to get friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan Taylor Swift to appear in a sketch about the show.
story: Mariska Hargitay seemingly used her pull as host of the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards to get friend and longtime “Law & Order: SVU” fan Taylor Swift to appear in a sketch about the show.

During the Sept. 14 awards show, the telecast cut to a pre-taped sketch featuring Hargitay, Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino and more actors playing their characters from the crime drama. Their case to crack: Will Taylor Swift attend the Emmys?
Each actor took turns suggesting why certain nominees and shows pointed toward Swift making a surprise appearance. Hargitay, as Olivia Benson, brought up as evidence Swift’s love of Easter eggs.
Suddenly, a crime board was wheeled away to reveal Swift was standing in the precinct.
“Hey guys, this isn’t adding up,” she said while wearing a gray suit  and holding a coffee mug.
When Ice-T asked her to explain her theory, she replied, “Our perp has a clear M.O. A lot of this doesn’t fit the pattern, and I don’t think everything is a clue.”
“It is to the Swifties,” Hargitay quickly replied.
The sketch continued to poke fun at Swift, whose cat — named Olivia Benson, after the TV character — also appeared in Swift’s arms.

Hargitay cracked the case by explaining that Swift couldn’t make it to the Los Angeles event because she’d be too busy supporting husband Travis Kelce at his Kansas City Chiefs game on Sept. 14 against Denver Broncos.
With the case solved, the iconic “SVU” “dun-dun” played.
“Oh, wow,” Swift said before sharing that the sound is her ring tone.
The segment ended with Hargitay and Swift dramatically staring into the camera while the show’s outro played.

title: Tyler Perry Shares Plans for a Big Move After His 57th Birthday
summary: Tyler Perry, known for building his entertainment empire in Atlanta, says he’s planning to move to Puerto Rico in 2027.
story: Tyler Perry has long been synonymous with Atlanta, the home base of his entertainment empire, but the movie and television mogul says he is about to make a big move after turning 57 years old.
Perry spoke with TODAY special correspondent Justin Sylvester on Sept. 14 about making a change as he reevaluates his priorities.
“Yes, I am officially — you’re the first to hear this — I am officially moving to Puerto Rico,” Perry said. “No, this is real.”
Perry, who is the father of an 11-year-old son with ex Gelila Bekele, expects to relocate to the U.S. territory in 2027.
“Yep, moving to Puerto Rico at the top of the year, and I’m pulling back a whole lot,” he told Sylvester.
Sylvester asked him what prompted the change.
“Oh, getting older,” Perry, who turned 57 on Sept. 13, said. “It’s time to slow down a little bit, enjoy more time with my son, and just take it all in.”
He said spending more time with his son Aman has also helped him with issues related to his own childhood trauma.
“Having this opportunity and this moment to be a father and give him all the love that I never had has been really, really healing,” Perry said.
Perry’s relationship with his son and his childhood trauma are examined in the 2023 documentary “Maxine’s Baby: The Tyler Perry Story,” which was co-directed by Bekele.
In the film, a then-8-year-old Aman asks his father why he works so hard.

“Why do I work so hard?” Perry responds. “Because I want you to have a really good future and I want us to have a really good life. We can travel and have fun and help other people. So, don’t you think that’s a good idea?”
“You’re my hero,” Aman answers.
“Aw, you’re my hero!” Perry replied. “I love you.”
In 2020, Perry confirmed he and Bekele had split after a long term relationship but called her an “incredible mother” in a 2022 interview with AARP the Magazine.
Perry has tried to keep his son out of the limelight.

“My son’s not famous,” he told AARP the Magazine. “I want him to have as normal a life as he can. “I want him to know what it’s like to have his own name and his own life and not have the pressure of trying to live up to whatever or whoever your father was.”

Before Perry gets to his move to Puerto Rico, the man with more than two dozen feature films and 17 television shows to his name is still as hard working as ever. He spoke to Sylvester about his new movie, “Why Did I Get Married Again?” which began streaming on Netflix on Sept. 9.

It’s the third installment of a trilogy that began in 2007 about a group of friends who are now in their 50s. The film series also helped Perry reach a conclusion in his own life, as his age mirrors those of the characters.

“When I wrote the first one I thought, ‘You know, marriage might be a good idea at some point,’” Perry said. “But at this age, I’m like, ‘No, that’s not a good idea for me.’ So, no. Won’t be any marriage for me.”

title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Season 35 Has a Unique Twist, Pro Witney Carson Breaks It Down
summary: “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 will include an unexpected elimination twist that hasn’t been done before. What to know ahead of the premiere.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
“Dancing With the Stars” is switching things up for Season 35 — and some people, including the pros, have thoughts.
The dancing competition show kicks off with a two-night premiere starting at 8 p.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 15 and again on Wednesday, Sept. 16.

Sixteen couples, including three with previous dance experience, will step out onto the ballroom floor for their first dance of the season. However, in a move that hasn’t been done since 2018, there will be a double elimination during premiere week.
So what’s the major twist for Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars”?

For night one, only the male celebrities will bust out their moves and perform a song from the year they were born. At the end of the Sept. 15 episode, one male star and their partner will be eliminated.

Night two will see the female celebrities show their skills on the dance floor, also dancing to the same theme. One female celebrity  will go home at the end of the Sept. 16 episode. This means two couples will be eliminated during week one.

“We haven’t done this before,” Witney Carson, Season 35 pro and reigning Mirrorball champion, tells TODAY.com. “It’s not really news to me that we change some things out. We stay to the core of what the show is, which is competing and dancing. All of that stays the same.”

The last time one male and female celebrity were eliminated during premiere week was during Season 26 when Olympic snowboarder Jamie Anderson and MLB star Johnny Damon were eliminated first. However, that season was condensed to a total of four episodes with only athletes competing.

“I think it’s very scary that there’s an elimination both nights because that usually doesn’t happen,” Carson, who is partnered with “Jimmy Kimmel Live!” personality Guillermo Rodriguez, says. “But at the same time, there’s a lot of couples and that’s just (the) competition. You have to vote people out, and I think people are going to have a really hard time doing that because every celebrity is so amazing.”

Fellow pro Mark Ballas also questioned whether the stars should be split into two groups based on gender. The dancer, who has competed in 22 “DWTS” seasons and is a three-time Mirrorball champ, also noted that he’s never experienced an elimination like this.
“I don’t think I was even on the show when that happened. This is a first,” he said on the Sept. 9 episode of the “Get Real” podcast, adding, “It’s not an even playing field, right?”
“It’s kind of like, boys over there, girls over there, one of you is going from each group. So that’s a little different,” he said, noting it adds pressure on the couples.
Carson, on her end, tells TODAY.com that she’s “trying to not let” the possibility of being eliminated after her first dance affect her her mindset.

“I think people are gonna have a tough time letting people go, and we will too,” she continued. “It’ll be horrible. The worst part of the show is letting people go. I wish we could all win. We’d all go to the finale.”
Who Is Competing on Night 1 of ‘DWTS’?
The first night will include a slew of male celebs, ranging from reality stars to actors to comedians and more.

The guys competing will be “The Bachelorette” alum Tyler Cameron, Paralympian Ezra French, singer Taylor Hanson, “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” star Conner Leavitt, Savannah Bananas player Jackson Olson, “Jimmy Kimmel Live” star Guillermo Rodriguez, actor Harry Shum Jr. and influencer Connor Wood.
Who Is Competing on Night 2 of ‘DWTS’?
The ladies will hold the fort down for night two.

Competing are “Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” alum Tatyana Ali, celebrity chef Giada De Laurentiis, actor Jenna Dewan, Olympian Amber Glenn, “Traitors” and “Love Island UK” star Maura Higgins, “Summer House” star Ciara Miller, reality star Sarah Jane Nader and actor Julia Stiles.
How Will Voting Work for the Two-Night ‘DWTS’ Premiere?
Voting will work a little differently for the Season 35 “DWTS” premiere.
Voting for each night will be open only for the couples who are competing in their respective episode: male celebrities on Tuesday and female celebrities on Wednesday, according to ABC.

Viewers will have the chance to cast their vote during the live simulcast of the show in the ET/CT time zones. At that time, online voting will be available to fans in any time zone in the U.S., its territories and Canada via dwtsvote.abc.com.
Additionally, fans in the U.S. also have the chance to vote via SMS/text. The couples’ numbers to text will be shared ahead of the episodes.
The live viewer votes will then be combined with scores the judges — Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough — give to determine who is eliminated after every episode.
Witney Carson Reminds Fans That Voting Is Essential
Since the couples only get one chance before they are at risk of being eliminated, Carson says voting is vital.

“It’s not enough time. If I had it my way, I would let everyone go through to the next week,” she says. “But there’s only so many weeks that we have. It’s tough (and) it just goes to show, you have to vote!”
“You have to vote for your favorites,” she continues. “People don’t realize the votes are really, really important. If you don’t vote, then they won’t stick around.”

title: What Time Are the Emmys? How to Watch the 2026 Awards Show
summary: The 78th Emmy Awards will see some of the biggest Hollywood stars going head to head in the major categories.
story: The 78th Emmy Awards will see some of the biggest Hollywood stars going head to head in the major categories.

The 2026 Emmy Awards, television’s biggest night, will be held on Monday, Sept. 14, in Los Angeles. The ceremony will be broadcast live from Peacock Theater and feature nominees like Zendaya, Oscar Isaac, Steve Carell, Colman Domingo and more.

Mariska Hargitay, who’s cemented her icon status for her portrayal of the beloved “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” protagonist Olivia Benson, will be hosting the ceremony.  It marks the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch in 2011.
Hargitay herself has already won two Creative Arts Emmys on Sept. 5 for her deeply-personal film “My Mom Jayne,” about her mother, screen legend Jayne Mansfield.
Nominations were first revealed on July 8, with TODAY exclusively sharing the nominees for outstanding variety series and outstanding reality competition program.

After all the categories were announced, “The Pitt” led with a staggering 25 nominations. “Hacks” closely followed with 24 nods for its fifth and final season, which set a record in the comedy category. Rounding out the top three was new series “Widow’s Bay” with 19 nominations.
There were also 28 actors who received their first-ever Emmy nominations. Some of them have already added “Emmy winner” to their resume, after taking home an award at the Creative Arts Emmys.
Soon, more stars will be presented with the coveted golden statue.
Read on to learn everything you need to know about the 2026 Emmys.
When Are the 2026 Emmys?
The 2026 Emmys are set to air live on Monday, Sept. 14, beginning at 5 p.m. PT/ 8 p.m. ET.
The ceremony will be held at Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
How to Watch and Stream the 2026 Emmys
The show will be broadcast from coast-to-coast on NBC and will stream live and on demand on Peacock, as well.
Nights one and two from the Creative Arts Emmys will air on FXX on Saturday, Sept. 12, at 8 p.m. ET/PT. It will be available to stream on Hulu the following day.
Who Is Hosting the 2026 Emmys?
The Television Academy announced in July that Mariska Hargitay will emcee the event.

Hargitay has already won two Emmys for her film “My Mom Jayne,” taking home outstanding documentary and outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program. The accolades make her a three-time Emmy winner.
Speaking about the honor during an appearance on TODAY in August, Hargitay shared that it took her a minute to process that she was being asked to host the major award show.
“I thought about it over the weekend and then I started going, ‘Why not?’” she recalled.

“Which is where I kind of am in my life,” the “Law & Order: SVU” star continued. “I was so incredibly honored and, again, knowing that it’s the first woman in 15 years was absolutely thrilling. And I am somebody to take on new challenges.”

title: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann’s Love Story, In Their Own Words
summary: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann met on the set of “Law & Order: SVU” and have been married for 22 years. Ahead of the Emmys, here’s what to know about their relationship.
story: Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann first met on the set of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.” Now, 22 years of marriage later, they are going as strong as ever.

Hargitay has had a big year. Her directorial debut, the documentary “My Mom Jayne” is up for an Emmy Award and she’s set to make her hosting debut as emcee of the Sept. 14 ceremony. She also made her Broadway debut in “Every Brilliant Thing.” Her final show on July 5 was a true family affair, with Hermann appearing on stage to propose to his wife’s character.
Hargitay and Hermann started dating shortly after their initial encounter in the early 2000s, and in 2004, they got married. They’ve since welcomed three kids: August, Amaya and Andrew.
In a March 2018 interview with People, Hargitay opened up about the life that she’s created with Hermann.
“My husband is my North Star, and my kids are my teachers,” she said.
“Our family is so perfect, or at least perfect for me,” Hargitay added. “Together we’re just this whole, happy, joyful, chaotic, crazy unit. I’ve never known anything that was more right.”
Here’s a timeline of Hargitay and Hermann’s relationship, and what they have said about each other and their family in interviews.
They Met on ‘Law & Order: SVU’ in 2001

Hargitay and Hermann met in November 2001, per InStyle, when he guest-starred on Season 3 of “Law & Order: SVU.” Hargitay plays Olivia Benson, now captain of the Manhattan Special Victims Unit, and Hermann played defense attorney Trevor Langan. Since then, he’s appeared in other episodes of the 27-season show.
During a January 2022 appearance on “The Drew Barrymore Show,” Hargitay recalled their first encounter and said that she was “nervous” to be around him because he was so “handsome.”
“It was distracting,” she said.
Hargitay noted that her first thought after meeting Hermann was, “Who is that Clark Gable Superman guy that I need to marry today?”

Hargitay laughed about how her friends kept telling her that she should put herself out there more because no one was just going to show up on “Law & Order: SVU” and marry her. To their surprise, and to hers, that’s exactly what happened.
Their First Date Was at Church
Months after meeting on “Law & Order: SVU,” Hargitay said that she and Hermann were having a discussion about religion, per InStyle. She said Hermann then asked her to go to church.
Faith is important to both Hargitay and Hermann.
“I think God is very much in us. Faith is a huge part of our life. And I think everything happens for a reason,” Hargitay told SF Gate.
During the sermon, Hargitay told TODAY she got emotional — not because of the church environment, but because of their connection.

“I cried because I was feeling something that I’d never felt before, but I kind of knew what it was and I always say people, well, you know, when you’re a little girl, your parents and your grandparents and everyone goes, ‘When you’re in love, you’ll know.’ And I did,” she said. “And before I did I’d never felt that. And so when I was sitting in church, it was so hilarious, because Peter was like, ‘Oh my God, she’s so moved.’”
They Got Married in 2004
In August 2004, Hargitay and Hermann got married in Santa Barbara, California, in front of 200 guests, per People.

“I think we both knew, sort of, what we found,” Hargitay later told People in 2019. “We sort of knew that we found the right one. I never thought it could be this good, and I never knew that I’d be reminded on the journey, that I’d marry the right one. That I waited and married the right one and it’s better than I thought it was. Because sometimes you take a snapshot and you go, ‘I can’t believe this is my life.’”
They Welcomed Son August in 2006
In June 2006, Hargitay and Hermann welcomed their first child, son August Miklos Friedrich Hermann.

“Nobody wanted to be pregnant more than me,” the “Lake Placid” star told SELF magazine in 2007. “From the minute I found out, I was wearing full-on maternity pants. My stomach was totally flat, mind you, but I was just so excited.”
In a 2019 interview with Traveling Mom, Hargitay said having a child made her and Hermann more “compassionate toward other people.”

“You go from being that person who would get annoyed at the sound of a crying baby, hoping it would just go to sleep, to the one who is completely empathic toward the parents, hoping the baby is OK and wondering if there is anything you can do to help,” she said. “Now, we’re all in the same boat. We’re on the same team, which is one of my favorite things about becoming a parent. I feel like I’m in the club now.”
They Adopted Daughter Amaya in April 2011
In April 2011, Hargitay and her hubby adopted daughter Amaya Josephine Hermann.

“I’m deliriously happy,” Hargitay told People at the time. “From the minute she was born, she was just surprisingly alert and so full of love.” According to People, the couple’s daughter was born in the United States.
Before Hermann and Hargitay adopted her, they were “considering both international and domestic adoption” for their second kid.
“We talked a lot about mixed-race adoptions, and we are very excited that we are now a multi-racial family. We’re just so happy she’s here,” Hargitay said.
As for August? The “Tales from Earthsea” star noted that the then 4-year-old took to being an older brother easily.
“He calls her his baby because he says the whole thing was his idea,” she said. “He always talks about how he’s going to protect her. He’s going to be a great big brother.”
... And They Adopted Son Andrew Months Later
In October 2011, Hargitay and Hermann adopted their third child, son Andrew Nicolas Hargitay Hermann, just months after they became parents to Amaya.
In an interview with People, Hargitay said that she barely had any clothes to give him because she gave all of August’s old clothes to her godson, who was born a few months before Andrew.
“It was so hilarious,” she said.
But thanks to her friends, Hargitay was able to clothe her baby in a few onesies that they brought over.

While Hargitay and Hermann were considering adopting another child, Andrew’s adoption came more quickly than anticipated. In an interview with Good Housekeeping, Hargitay explained they received word of a premature child and that saying yes was a “no-brainer.”
“It was like … a miracle. And I don’t use that word lightly. I’ve never made a bigger decision so quickly,” Hargitay aid.
Once the paperwork was finalized, Hargitay told People they felt “so lucky” to be parents again.

“We never in a million years thought it would happen this quickly, but something inside of us knew that this was right, and we said, ‘Yes, yes, yes!’” she explained to People. “We knew this was our guy. Everything about it felt right. It felt divinely right.”
After taking Andrew home, Hargitay felt more joy than she could ever imagine.
“I always describe it as this angel that fell out of the sky, because he was a little unexpected,” she told People in 2019.

“It’s something that happened very quickly, when adoption can take a long time,” Hargitay added. “We were so beautifully and surprisingly … not because we’re not in sync, but surprisingly in sync about something so huge. So momentous.”
They Just Celebrated Their 22nd Anniversary
In August 2026, Hargitay and Hermann celebrated their 22-year wedding anniversary.
To commemorate the occasion, Hargitay shared a black-and-white photo of them in Cannes, France, seemingly from 2025, when she debuted “My Mom Jayne” at the city’s film festival.
“Happy 22nd anniversary Peter Hermann. You’ve got all my love,” she captioned the photo.
Mariska Hargitay Revealed How She Keeps Her Marriage So ‘New and Fresh’

Amid their 20th wedding anniversary, when asked how she keeps their marriage so “fresh,” Hargitay told Jenna Bush Hager on TODAY with Hoda & Jenna that it has everything to do with how she views their romance.

“I’m at a point in my life where it just keeps getting better with him. And marriage is not always like this,” Hargitay said, while putting her arm in an upright position, “or any relationship that is deep in matters. But, I have learned so much.”

“Peter always says this beautiful quote about ... breaking through marriage into marriage,” she continued. “And that is what I think we’ve lived because at this time in my life, I feel very different than I have for the last maybe 15 or 18 — and I feel (assured) up in our love.”
Mariska Hargitay and Peter Hermann Have Brought Their Kids to Red Carpets

While rare, Hargitay and Hermann occasionally bring their three kids to red carpets, including in May 2023, when the whole family attended the Stuttering Association for the Young Benefit Gala in New York City.
Hargitay and Hermann have been outspoken about August, now 20, and his stutter. Both actors were inducted into the Stuttering Association for the Young’s Hall of Fame.
“It’s been so exciting to learn and to understand and educate people because as soon as people know, they’re like, ‘Oh, my gosh. Thank you. Tell me more. Tell me more,’” Hargitay told People in 2023.
In 2025, Hargitay brought August, Amaya and Andrew along for several red carpet events for her film “My Mom Jayne,” including its debut at Cannes Film Festival and its New York City premiere.
Peter Hermann Proposes To Mariska Hargitay (For A Second Time)

At Hargitay’s closing night performance of “Every Brilliant Thing,”  an interactive one-person play and Hargitay’s Broadway debut, Hermann filled an audience-participant role given to someone in the crowd.
The role of Sam, the character’s childhood best friend and eventual spouse, was played by Hermann during Hargitay’s July 5 show.
Hermann got down on one knee to act out a proposal, which received lots of laughter and cheers from the audience.
Hargitay and Hermann shared an on-stage hug and a kiss to close out her Broadway run.
Peter Hermann Plays Plus One At Creative Arts Emmys Awards
Mariska Hargitay took home two trophies at the Creative Arts Emmys Awards on Sept. 5.
Peter Hermann, adorned in an all-black suit, walked the red carpet with Hargitay following the ceremony, and the two posed together with her hardware.

For her documentary “My Mom Jayne,” Hargitay won outstanding documentary or nonfiction special. From her role as director, she also secured the win for outstanding directing for a documentary/nonfiction program.

title: Our 1 Big Question for Mariska Hargitay During Commercial: How Does It Feel to Be Mariska Hargitay?
summary: Mariska Hargitay opens up about the healing she found in making “My Mom Jayne,” hosting the Emmys and how Knicks point guard, Jalen Brunson, has inspired her.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.

In Hollywood, there are A-listers and then there’s royalty. Mariska Hargitay lands in the latter category. The daughter of screen legend Jayne Mansfield, Hargitay has followed in her mother’s footsteps, becoming luminary in her own right for her portrayal of Olivia Benson on “Law & Order: SVU.”
It’s a role that’s earned her both an Emmy and a Golden Globe. Not to mention that, at 27 years and counting, it’s the longest-running primetime series in NBC history.

On this day, however, Hargitay hasn’t come to unpack the latest season of the crime drama. Instead, we sit down in TODAY’s Orange Room to talk about the latest season of her life, a chapter that’s been especially fulfilling for a number of reasons.

Among them? She’s just wrapped her successful Broadway debut, sat courtside with bestie Taylor Swift before her beloved Knicks took home the championship, and premiered the deeply personal film “My Mom Jayne,” which earned the 62-year-old yet another an Emmy nomination.

If she wins, she won’t have far to go to pick up the trophy since Hargitay is also hosting the Emmys this year, the first time a woman has hosted the awards show since Jane Lynch held the distinction back in 2011.

It’s undoubtedly Hargitay’s moment. The actor reflects on the “profound healing” that got her here and how the Knicks’ Jalen Brunson played a part in it. She also delves into her work with the Purple Leash Project, a partnership between Purina and the nonprofit RedRover that spotlights the need for more pet-friendly domestic violence shelters, an initiative near and dear to her heart.
This interview has been lighted edited for clarity.
First of all, I just want to acknowledge the fact that I didn’t think about it either and that’s what hit me so hard when I learned about it, because I don’t think anybody thinks about that.

So, it’s a really powerful and extraordinary initiative. Just the idea that a survivor shouldn’t have to choose between her safety and her animals. There’s already so many barriers of why not to leave and why not to go, but this one is a huge one.

This idea that pets are actually family members and oftentimes the most consistent, steady presence in a survivor’s life, that provides so much comfort, so much support, so much safety, really. And here was a reason that people weren’t going.

Up to 50% of survivors were not wanting to go, to leave their animals. So, it’s actually a brilliant initiative to a way of  supporting survivors. It takes that off their plate and they’re doing it all over and I was just so moved by it and so happy to get on board.

They’re like your children. They are an extended part of your family. Also, the idea of animals being used as threats or used as tactics to keep the person there or threaten that if they leave, they’ll hurt the animal. More than 70% of women in shelters report that their abuser has used an animal as a form of control.
So, it’s innovative, brilliant and so survivor-centric. And it is truly something that supports healing and gives survivors the courage to leave and supports them in a profound way.

I’ll tell you what it feels like: When I made this film, everything changed. I think the way I described it is finding so much more internal space that I didn’t have. It really settled my nervous system and was very profoundly healing for me in ways I was aware of, and in ways that I wasn’t.

My friend Kelli Giddish, my amazing co-star, had said to me after she saw (“My Mom Jayne”), because she knows me very well, she says, “I can’t wait to see what you do next,” and that really resonated with me really deeply.
For me, it wasn’t an accident that all this ... it was like a pathway started opening up because I think, and I’ve always believed, that the only way out is through. That’s sort of my motto.
This is also why I made this film, this is why I did that. Because I was carrying something that I didn’t want to carry and I realized, wasn’t mine to carry.

So, in a way, yes, I’m doing all these amazing things and I’m doing all these new things. In a way, it’s surprising and sort of unbelievable. And in a way, it feels like, “Of course. Now.” Because I’ve gotten ready for it internally.

I’ve always been a person to take on new challenges, but the fact that these opportunities are coming – I think that something shifted. So when the play came, I was 62. My mother was 22 (when she made her Broadway debut), and I made this film. So, I just believed that it wasn’t an accident that after I made the film, it sort of cleared that out and dealt with it and had a new reconciliation and new peace with it and so much new discovery.
So, the fact that the play came, I went, “Of course it did.” And I feel a little bit like that with the Emmys. As much as it was a shocker for me, I went, “Got it.”
